is complete. The closer's `done`, when the last line names the closer, is what completes it,
and the close sits in the same commit.

1. Move `open/m-<tid>.md` and its bodies, `open/m-<tid>-*.md`, to `closed/`.

## What is not here

- No inbox file. What is pending for a member is a query over `open/`, so a lost or stale inbox
  cannot disagree with the threads.
- No counter file per thread. The next number is read from the thread itself.
- No format version in the lines. The README's version is the rules', fields are additive,
  and a reader takes what is there.
- No second machine. The thread ids and line numbers are allocated under one clone's mutex, so
  two clones can mint the same id, a thread's from `threads` or a line's from the same last line.
  The rejected push catches it and the loser renumbers, which is why an id is final only once
  pushed. A second clone that never collides means member-scoped ids for threads and lines both,
  and that is the change it would take.
- No access control. Any member can modify or delete any file here. It works among friendly
  participants, and history is the only recourse.
- No commit per line. Under one clone the mutex is what keeps writes from interleaving, and a
  line's author and time are in the line, so a commit adds only the link to the session that
  wrote it. Committing batches lines, pushing backs them up, and the version commit is the one
  commit the rules require.
- No archive. `closed/` grows by a file per thread and its bodies, and git and `rg` carry that
  far past this family's traffic. The technique comes when it matters, a directory per year or a
  store outside the tree, and the ids, never reused, survive either.

## Versions

The title carries the rules' version, and the tree is always at that version: the commit that
bumps it edits this file and rewrites `open/` and `closed/` to the new shape in the same commit,
under the mutex, with every member's last push already in `main@origin`. History is never
rewritten, so a reader supports one shape, the one this file describes, and a tool that finds
the title behind it says so rather than parsing the past.

- v0.3.3: a commit is titled with the ids of the threads it touches, `m-3 m-4`, a close
  included, so the close form and the line-id form go. The first batch under v0.3.2 carried five
  lines across two threads and five ids read as noise, and a commit that closed two threads had
  no title form, iiac-perf's finding at `m-3-1`. The title is a convenience, never a store, and
  the diff says what the commit did in each thread.
- v0.3.2: a commit that closes a thread is titled `close m-<tid> <title>` whatever lines it
  carries, and a title that lists ids is for a batch that closes nothing. The first close under
  v0.3.1, `13a7d9f7`, carried six lines, and six ids read as noise where the close is the event.
- v0.3.1: no blank line under the heading, so line `<num>` is file line `<num>` plus two, closed
  threads move to `closed/` instead of being deleted, a commit may carry any number of actions,
  the close in the same commit as its last `done`, and a release may leave lines uncommitted, so
  the clean-working-copy guard is gone and a commit batches whatever the working copy holds. A
  member's own line, of either action, clears what was pending for them, so a reply needs no
  `done` after it, `done` is the empty reply, and `read` is retired, since a line that clears
  nothing has no place in a query over lines. From the `m-2` replies: addressed means the
  recipient field alone, a reply answers everything it clears, naming each, and `owner`'s times
  are UTC to the second. The migration restored `m-1` from history without its blank line, its
  surplus `done` marks still valid lines.
- v0.3.0, the cutover from v0.2.0's records and inboxes: every record was complete, so no
  thread carried over. `threads` was created at 0, `notices.md`, `topics/`, the inboxes,
  `README-old.md`, and the `.owner` copy of the mutex were deleted, and the draft became this
  file. The v0.2.0 tree is the tag `v0.2.0`, and `git log -S'<heading>'` finds a record.

## Specimen

`open/m-41.md`, opened by abc to def and ghi, answered by both, and complete: ghi's line at 1
and def's at 2 are above 0, the line naming them, and abc's `done` at 3 is above 1 and 2, the
lines naming abc. `threads` holds 41 or more. Line 2 has a body, `open/m-41-2.md` beside it,
shown after it.

```

- m-41-0 2026-09-09T16:00:00Z from abc to def,ghi hello
- m-41-1 2026-09-09T16:05:42Z from ghi to abc hi
- m-41-2 2026-09-09T16:09:12Z from def to abc [hey, and the cycle that answers it](m-41-2.md)
- m-41-3 2026-09-09T16:12:30Z from abc done
```

1	# Todo list
2	
3	This file contains near term tasks with a short description and reference links to more details.
4	Its shape is [Todo format](agent-data/notes.md#todo-format).
5	
6	The other files:
7	
8	- [BUGS.md](BUGS.md): List of vc-x1 bugs that should be addressed 
9	- [zDOING.md](zDOING.md): the cycle being worked on, its planning and its work's documentation,
10	  and the continuation notes a session leaves for the next.
11	- [zCLOSED.md](zCLOSED.md): the last finished cycle's record, kept until the next one closes.
12	- [bugs.md](notes/bugs.md): the bugs.
13	
14	## Waiting
15	
16	Important work that cannot start yet. Each entry names what it waits on, in a form that can be
17	checked, and the rank it takes in `## Todo` once unblocked. Every opening checks each condition
18	and promotes what is met ([Opening](AGENTS.md#opening)).
19	
20	- **Retire the frozen history: `notes/chores/` and `notes/done.md`.** (wink, 2026-08-27) They
21	  are frozen and no longer grow, and the agent-repo transcript plus git history hold what they
22	  hold. Delete both in one cycle, after a sweep turns every link into them (Todo entries, the
23	  backlog, rationale.md, the other members' messages) into a permalink at the SHA before the
24	  deletion.
25	  - Waits on: **`vc-x1 closed "<title>"`** landed, and the session viewer good enough to read
26	    a cycle's record from the transcript.
27	  - Place when unblocked: first.
28	- **Sync's remote look stops spawning git.** (wink + agent, 2026-10-09) Sync learns where a
29	  remote's bookmarks are by spawning `git ls-remote`, and downloads the commits of the ones that
30	  moved by spawning a `git fetch` that moves no ref, the sixth entry of the spawn register in
31	  `clippy.toml` and the one spawn of `git`. Replace `git_command` and its two callers in
32	  `src/jj/session.rs` with jj-lib's query, delete the `#[allow]`, and close the entry.
33	  - Waits on: jj-lib's public API offering that query. Neither 0.45.1 nor 0.46.0 has one:
34	    `rg -i 'ls.remote' src/` in the jj-lib source prints nothing, and its git subprocess layer is
35	    `pub(crate)`. An upstream feature request, once filed or found, is named here.
36	  - Place when unblocked: first, being one function.
37	
38	## Todo
39	
40	Entries are in priority order, the first highest, and reprioritizing is moving an entry. Each is a
41	`###` heading, so a citation is a link to its anchor. Long-tail entries live in
42	[todo-backlog.md](notes/todo-backlog.md). Use the [Prose form](agent-data/prose.md#prose-form).
43	Deeper detail goes in a `notes/` design file (link via `[N]` ref).
44	
45	### custom.md is optional and never committed
46	
47	(wink + agent, 2026-10-17) A project's `custom.md` holds what is true of one machine, the family's
48	paths and the session's standing permissions, so committing it makes every clone assume a
49	development environment that exists only here. The family is local: no repo assumes one, and the
50	layer a member shares with its family lives with the family, not in the member's repo.
51	
52	- `custom.md` is gitignored and untracked, and the agent reads it when there is one: the rule
53	  **Read custom.md first**, [Acquaint](AGENTS.md#acquaint)'s first step, and
54	  [custom.md](AGENTS.md#custommd) say so, and the last says it is local.
55	- A project convention that must be committed goes into the agent-file it belongs to, its diff

Agreed. Making the untracking the cycle's goal is a better shape than the one in `zCLOSED.md` now. Here's how I'd reshape it.

**Why it fits now**
- The commit hasn't been pushed and has no bookmark, so the cycle record can be rewritten freely.
- The `.gitignore` change already in the working copy is the actual change. The five Todo entries are its documentation and the follow-on plan, which is what a single-step cycle carries in one commit.
- It's convention work, so it can't be bundled into a feature cycle. It doesn't need to be: this cycle becomes the convention cycle.

**How `zCLOSED.md` would change**
- **Title**: something like `chore: custom.md is untracked and gitignored`. The current title describes only the Todo entries, which become the smaller part.
- **Problem**: this is a public repo meant for anyone to clone, and they won't be family members. A committed `custom.md` gives every clone a layer for one machine: the family's sibling paths and your standing permissions.
- **Deliberation**: keep what's there (the family is local, the abandoned family-directory bookmark, fixtures named by their source) and add:
  - Untracking comes first. Fixing the agent-files wording comes in a later proposal cycle.
  - The file stays on disk here and is gone from the tree from this commit on. Older commits still hold it, and it contains nothing sensitive.
- **Solution**: `custom.md` is untracked and in `.gitignore`, and the five entries open `## Todo`. The first entry shrinks: its "gitignored and untracked" bullet is now done, so what remains is the `AGENTS.md` wording ("read it when there is one") and the open question of whether the template ships an example file.
- **Acceptance check**:
  - `git ls-files custom.md` prints nothing after the commit, and `custom.md` is still on disk.
  - `vc-x1 validate` passes.
  - The real test of "anyone can clone it": clone it fresh into `tmp/` and run `cargo build` and `cargo test` there. I'm not sure whether `vc-x1 validate-anchors` follows `AGENTS.md`'s links to `custom.md`. If it does, it would fail in a fresh clone, and the check would show that.

**Caveats to state honestly in the record**
- **"Just works" holds for building and testing, not yet for the agent.**
  - `AGENTS.md` still says "Read custom.md first" with no "if there is one", so an agent in a fresh clone gets an instruction it can't follow. That's what Todo entry 1 fixes.

158-The mechanics behind [Cycles run on a bookmark](../AGENTS.md#cycles-run-on-a-bookmark). That section

161-
162-**Create**, at the cycle's opening, with the bookmark named by the cycle title's slug (the anchor
163-algorithm in [Markdown anchor links](notes.md#markdown-anchor-links), so the block's title heading
164-and the bookmark derive from one bare title):
165-
166-- `jj git push --named <bookmark>=@- -R .` is the common case: it creates the bookmark at the last
167-  committed change and publishes it in one invocation.
168-- Any other revision works as the `=<rev>` right-hand side. When `<rev>` is not `@-`, follow with
169-  `jj new <rev> -R .` so the working copy actually sits on the new line. Otherwise the bookmark
170-  exists and the next commit lands somewhere else.
171-- `jj bookmark set <bookmark> -r <rev> -R .` creates it without publishing, for a line that is not
172-  ready to be seen.
173-
174-**Land**, once the close-out is approved: the sequence that makes the cycle permanent, begun by a
175-sync that found `main` unmoved ([Sync](../AGENTS.md#sync)). Every
176-`jj git push` in it is a push under [Approval per push](../AGENTS.md#before-any-push) and [Hard

178-closing words before the final invocation, silence after ([At
179-rest](../AGENTS.md#at-rest-push-stop-squash-push)):

182-   name](versioning.md#dev-artifact-name)): rename `<name>-dev` back to `<name>` in the manifest,
183-   `vc-x1 validate --fast` so the lockfile follows, and `jj squash` folds the edit into the closing
184-   (`@` sits directly above it).

187-   as it is.

content.content:
### Conventional-commit shape (ladder / commit)

([why](rationale.md#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--commit))

A ladder step and its commit description share a *title* shape, a [Conventional
Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/) title (`<type>: <desc>`, an optional
`(scope)` after the type: `feat(push): ...`) over [Prose form](#prose-form) detail. They differ in
the title's marker (below) and in bullet *content*: commit bodies take the [Commit-body
form](#commit-body-form), the ladder's are conceptual (see "Bullet *content* differs by surface"
above). The shared template:

```
<title>                          # <title> is the commit's `<type>: <desc>`
<optional prose intro>
  - <optional item>
    <optional prose intro>
      - <optional sub-item>
      ...
```

The two surfaces apply it as:

- **Ladder step** (`TODO.md` `## In Progress`): the rung is `- [<title>][M] (marker)`: the title
  reference-linked to the rung's subsection via `[M]: #<slug>` in the file's `# References` (the
  closing rung linked like the rest), and the `(current)` / `(done)` marker. Its position in the
  list is its position in the ladder. The last rung is the close-out and its text says so. Detail
  lives not on the rung but in its subsection under the ladder, headed by the rung's exact
  title (see the protocol's [Opening](../AGENTS.md#opening)), bulleted, never `;`-joined inline.
- **Commit description**: no prefix. The title is the first line, and the body is the prose (see
  [Commit description](../AGENTS.md#commit-description)).

The title is **identical** across both for a given step, so a step's ladder entry and its commit
title line up verbatim. The rung's subsection heading carries the same title, a third
surface on every rung (the closing rung's exists only when close-out gotchas occurred: see the
protocol's [Opening](../AGENTS.md#opening)). Pick the commit title first and reuse it.
...
A scope names a component as its user would name it (a subcommand, a repo), never a file or
directory, and is omitted when there is none. A declared type's scope slot carries its
declaration's vocabulary instead ([Project-declared types](#project-declared-types)).

#### Project-declared types

Beyond the common types, a project may declare its own when a recurring kind of work deserves one
searchable token. The declaration names the type, its scope vocabulary, and its description
grammar, so a reader can parse the titles and a title check can admit them by name, and the scope
slot then carries what the declaration says rather than a component. A project's own declarations
live in its `custom.md`, and the set declares for itself:

- `agent-files`, the set's own lifecycle: `agent-files(<scope>): vX.Y.Z`, the description being the
  agent-files version in its `v` spelling ([Agent-files
  version](versioning.md#agent-files-version)), which keeps the formulaic titles unique and is the
  one version a title may carry ([Versions live in the version-of-record
  only](#versions-live-in-the-version-of-record-only)).
  - The two scopes:
    - `proposal`, outbound work for others to adopt. The cycle bumps the agent-files version, and
      the title names the new one.
    - `adoption`, inbound. The cycle copies the source's version file, and the title names what it
      took.
  - Who proposed to whom, or adopted from whom, is the message record's `from:` and `to:`, never
    the title's.
  - `git log --grep 'agent-files('` finds every agent-files title, the recurring type being the
    token that collects the thread.

### Steps are named, not numbered

A step has a title and no number. Nothing in a ladder rung or a commit gives a step an ordinal: a
rung's place in the list already *is* its place in the ladder, so a number beside it would restate
the position and then have to be maintained.

- **The title is the identifier.** A record points at a step by its title, a plain greppable
  mention, which is why the title is verbatim-identical across the three surfaces.
- **Unambiguous, not globally unique.** Two titles must be distinguishable where a title is
...
[why](rationale.md#agent-files-version)).

- **Record**: an empty file, `agent-data/agent-files-vX.Y.Z{-suffix}`, the version its name. `ls
  agent-data` shows it without a read, a bump is a rename, and
  `git log --diff-filter=A -- 'agent-data/agent-files-v*'` lists every version beside the commit
  that introduced it.
- **Spelling**: `vX.Y.Z` everywhere the agent-files version is written, the file name, an
  `agent-files` title, and vc-x1's output, so `agent-files v0.1.0` reads the same in all three. The
  `v` is the name-plus-version pair as cargo prints it (`bar v1.0.0`), and a tool's own banner stays
  bare (`vc-x1 0.82.0`), so a `v` number is the set's and a bare one the artifact's.
- **Proposals bump, adoptions copy**: a proposal cycle bumps it at the opening, advancing per
  [Advancing X.Y.Z](#advancing-xyz-patch-by-default), and its rungs walk the [Suffix
  scheme](#suffix-scheme) beside the artifact's version, `-0`, `-1`, then bare at the close-out, so
  a set copied from a draft bookmark says on its face that it is unfinished. An adoption copies the
  source's bare file and bumps nothing.
- **An adoption is a copy and a check**: `vc-x1 agent-files copy -c <src>` takes the set and the
  family's `custom.md` with it, and `vc-x1 agent-files diff -c <src>` is the adoption's last act,
  exiting zero when the two copies are the same. An adopter that keeps a `custom.md` of its own
  drops the `-c` from both, which is its prerogative.
- **Agreed**: the payload's number is the family's agreed version. An adopter ahead of it is
  proposing, one behind has not re-synced, and two proposers claiming one number are settled by the
  maintainer at convergence, the loser re-proposing under the next.
- **Which digit**: tend toward the patch digit, kept to one digit and rolled over into the minor.
  We think the minor stays within two digits and major increments when the family decides.

`custom.md` until the proposal cycle, and the committed config still names this machine's sibling
paths until the family and fixture entries land.

content.text:
A clone test that installs is the right proof that "anyone can clone this". It checks that the committed tree builds and installs with its own `Cargo.lock`, without `custom.md` and without this machine's working copy. Two things need settling first.

**1. What gets cloned.** The commit doesn't exist yet. The work is still uncommitted in `@`, and the bookmark points at `main`, so cloning the remote now would test the old tree. Three options:
- **Clone the local repo (my pick).** Put a temporary local bookmark on `@`, never pushed (`jj bookmark set ... -r @`), and clone this directory from `tmp/`:
  - `jj git clone`, then check out that bookmark.
  - `vc-x1 clone ./...`. Its source accepts a local path (`src/clone.rs:1`). It also tries to clone the agent-repo, and I'm not sure what it derives for that from a local path. If it trips there, that's a finding in itself.
  - Delete the temporary bookmark afterwards.
- **Test after the push.** This is the most real test, cloning from GitHub, but the result then lands after the commit. Recording it would be a late tweak to a pushed commit, which needs your approval like any push.
- **Do both.** Local before the push, and a remote check at Land as confirmation.

**2. The `vc-x1-test` rename and `--locked`.** Renaming the package in the clone's `Cargo.toml` makes `cargo install --locked` fail, because the lockfile's root entry still says `vc-x1`. Fixing the lockfile first would defeat the point of `--locked`, which is to prove the committed lock is consistent. Two ways around it:
- **Install the unmodified clone into a scratch directory (my pick):** `cargo install --path . --locked --root tmp/<clone>-install`. The binary is still called `vc-x1`, but it lands in `tmp/`, so `~/.cargo/bin/vc-x1` is never touched. This tests exactly what a stranger would get.
- **If you want the name `vc-x1-test` on your PATH:** do the same `--root` install and copy the binary as `vc-x1-test` (`--root` itself is still needed to keep `~/.cargo/bin/vc-x1` safe). Renaming the package itself is the dev-name mechanism the cycle protocol uses, which does regenerate the lock, and that's a different test.

**Smaller points**
- Run `cargo install` only after checking `custom.md` is absent from each clone, so the record can say the build didn't depend on it. I believe the build doesn't read it: only `src/agent_files/` mentions it, and only at run time.
- Add `cargo test` to the same two clones. Then the `jj git clone` case shows the jj side passes, and a plain `git clone` would reproduce the new `cli_smoke` Todo entry. I'd leave the plain-git case out of this cycle's checks, as you said.
- The acceptance check would gain one bullet: "A `jj git clone` and a `vc-x1 clone` of the commit's tree each `cargo install --path . --locked --root <scratch>` cleanly, and neither holds `custom.md`."

The plain version: clone this local repo twice in `tmp/`, once with `jj git clone` and once with `vc-x1 clone`, using a throwaway local bookmark on the uncommitted change. Install each with `--root` into a scratch folder rather than renaming, so `--locked` still means something and your real `vc-x1` isn't overwritten.

`vc-x1 clone` doesn't take a branch. `src/clone.rs` always clones the default branch and then requires `main` to be tracked (`verify_tracking(target_dir, "main")`). There's no `-b`/`--bookmark` option, and the target can't carry a branch name.

It doesn't need one, though. A clone fetches every remote bookmark, so after the push the cycle's bookmark is already in the clone as `chore-custommd-is-untracked-and-gitignored@origin`. The test becomes:

1. `vc-x1 clone https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1 vc-clone` in `tmp/acc`. This clones `main` plus the agent-repo; I'll take the URL from `origin` when we run it.
2. `jj new chore-custommd-is-untracked-and-gitignored@origin` in the clone.
3. Check there's no `custom.md`, then `cargo install --path . --locked --root ../vc-install`.

A `--bookmark <name>` option for `vc-x1 clone`, which would check out the bookmark and track it, is a nice-to-have for a Todo entry, not a blocker.

**When to run it.** A single-step cycle's record is finished inside its one commit, so a check that needs the pushed commit can't put its result there. Two choices:
- **After the push, before Land (my pick).** Run the three steps against the bookmark. A pass is reported to you. A failure is a finding: it gets a Todo entry, and it's your call whether it holds up Land. The record says this check runs after the push and is reported, not recorded.
- **At Land, after `main` is fast-forwarded.** A plain `vc-x1 clone` then gets this commit with no `jj new` step. But by then the commit is already permanent, so a failure can only become a Todo entry.

**Recording the checks**
- The `jj git clone` result can go in the record now as a pass: no `custom.md`, and the `--root` install gave `vc-x1 0.85.2 (agent-files v0.2.9)`, as you saw.
- `vc-x1 clone` of a local jj workspace fails because the source's git `HEAD` is detached, so the clone has no tracked `main`. That's a real bug, since the help lists local paths as sources. It gets a Todo entry, along with the `--bookmark` idea.

**Cleanup before the commit**
- Delete the local `acceptance-local` bookmark. It was never pushed, but a stray local bookmark would confuse a later look.
- Remove `tmp/acc` after your review. It's gitignored, but it holds two builds.

The plain version: `vc-x1 clone` has no branch option, but every clone already contains the bookmark, so after the push you clone, run `jj new <bookmark>@origin`, and install. Record the jj-clone pass now, run the `vc-x1 clone` test after the push and report it, and file the local-path bug and a `--bookmark` option in `TODO.md`.

136:### Commit-body form
137-
138-The specimen is [commit-model.md](commit-model.md). A commit body is the [Problem-first
139-shape](#problem-first-shape) with one addition: a body whose
140-problem has several sub-problems arranges them by a fixed recursion, so a reader knows what any
141-bullet is from its marker and its depth. The earlier statement, "a problem statement then a solution
142-statement, both broad", left that arrangement to taste, and taste converged slowly and separately.
143-
144-- **An intro paragraph states the general problem**, and defines any word the title assumes. It is
145-  mandatory. [Prose form](#prose-form) wants it regardless, and a body opening on a bullet is a body
146-  a `--body` flag can mistake for an option. The problem is *this commit's*, never the cycle's: the
147-  cycle's problem lives in the In Progress block, and a body whose problems outnumber what the diff
148-  resolves is describing something larger than the commit.
149-- **`*` bullets are the problem's facets**: sub-problems that decompose the intro's general problem,
150-  not a grab-bag of unrelated fixes. A body reaching for unrelated problem bullets is usually asking
151-  to be more than one commit.
152-- **`-` bullets are solutions**, and every `-` sits under a `*`, solving that facet. A `-` with no
153-  `*` above it reads as a solution to nothing, so there are no top-level solutions: a solution that
154-  retires every facet at once is written under each, or the facets are one.
155-- **One facet is the trivial commit**: the intro, one `*`, one or more `-` under it. Not a second
156-  form, the general form at its smallest.
157-- **A bookend body is a pointer**: an opening or closing commit resolves no problem of its own, so
158-  its body is the intro paragraph alone, naming the cycle by its title and pointing at its record,
159-  the In Progress block. No `*`, no `-`.
160-
161-**The markers are typed on purpose**: `*` always means problem, `-` always means solution, and the
162-pairing is what a reader counts on: the `-` answers the `*` above it, with no rule to consult. The
163-typing also keeps history greppable (`^\* ` finds every facet, `^ - ` every solution). Bodies are
164-read as plain text, in `jj log` and in terminals, where the markers survive, and if a renderer ever
165-flattens them the indentation still carries the structure. So the mixed markers are deliberate, and
166-a linter's consistent-marker rule is wrong to normalize them.
====
# Commit model

Two commit bodies from the `config loader` cycle in [cycle-model.md](cycle-model.md), shown as
specimens rather than a skeleton: a work rung's body and a bookend's. Copy the shape, not the
words. The rules are in [Commit-body form](prose.md#commit-body-form).

## A work rung

Title: `refactor: split loader from parser`

```
Config loading and parsing are one function, so the CLI cannot load a
config without parsing it and a test cannot parse one without a file on
disk. The move into its own module is what forces the split.

* The two jobs share one function and one error type.
  - `config::loader` finds and reads the file and returns the text with
    its path, so a caller that only wants to know which file was read
    stops there.
  - `config::parser` takes text and returns the schema, so a test hands
    it a string and never touches the filesystem.
* `main` still reaches into the parse result by field.
  - `main` calls `config::load` and receives the schema, so the field
    access moves behind the module boundary and the CLI no longer knows
    the file's shape.
```

The intro states this commit's problem and defines "split", the word the title assumes. Each `*`
is one facet of it, each `-` under a `*` answers that facet, and nothing names a file that the
diff already lists.

## A bookend

Title: `refactor: extract config loader opening`

```
Opens the cycle "refactor: extract config loader". Its record is the
In Progress block in TODO.md.
```

A bookend resolves no problem of its own, so its body is the intro paragraph alone, naming the
cycle by its title and pointing at its record. The closing's body is the same shape with "Closes".

# jj and cross-repo linking

How version control is driven on this project (jj, never raw git) and how the two repos' commits
point at each other (the `ochid:` trailer). Read this before any jj operation beyond `st` / `log` /
`diff`, and always before touching a commit description.

Universal file, shared with the template repository. A proposed change is edited here and converges
at the template ([Changing the agent-files](../AGENTS.md#changing-the-agent-files)). Project-local
content goes in [custom.md](../custom.md).

## jj Basics
...
# The session lock

An optional rule, off unless a project's [custom.md](../custom.md) turns it on: an agent session
holds an exclusive `flock` on `.agent-running` at the workspace root for as long as it runs, so a
second session started in the same workspace stops at its acquaint.

Universal file, shared with the template repository. A proposed change is edited here and converges
at the template ([Changing the agent-files](../AGENTS.md#changing-the-agent-files)). Project-local
content goes in [custom.md](../custom.md).

## The instruction

Turning the lock on is two edits: this entry goes into
`custom.md > ## Project conventions and overrides`, first in its list and in place of the entry
that says the lock is off, and `/.agent-running` goes into the work-repo's `.gitignore`.

...
  form *after* it, and reinterprets a lone `-N` as a post-release. Opposite directions, so no
  cross-medium logic may compare stored versions. Ordering truth lives in the ladder and git
  history. Comparing the public triple alone (e.g. a version gate) is unaffected.
- **`+` is reserved** for the PEP 440 remap: no SemVer build-metadata use in Rust repos even though
  Cargo allows it, since spending `+` there breaks the bijection with the Python spelling. A repo
  that truly needs it declares the deviation in its `custom.md`.

## Recording the version-of-record
Beyond the common types, a project may declare its own when a recurring kind of work deserves one
searchable token. The declaration names the type, its scope vocabulary, and its description
grammar, so a reader can parse the titles and a title check can admit them by name, and the scope
slot then carries what the declaration says rather than a component. A project's own declarations
live in its `custom.md`, and the set declares for itself:

- `agent-files`, the set's own lifecycle: `agent-files(<scope>): vX.Y.Z`, the description being the

content.text:
The sweep is mechanical, about 40 mentions in 9 files. The real work is two design questions it forces. I'd settle those before opening the cycle.

**What changes**

1. **One rule, written in one place.** `AGENTS.md > ## custom.md` shrinks to roughly: "When a `custom.md` exists at the workspace root, the agent reads it first, and it overrides anything in the agent-files." The rules index and Acquaint step 1 just link to that section.
   - The mention is plain code, `custom.md`, not a `[custom.md](custom.md)` link. Today's links break in every clone, since the file is no longer tracked.
2. **The custom.md boilerplate goes.** Seven `agent-data/` files carry "Project-local content goes in custom.md". That clause is dropped, leaving "Universal file … converges at the template".
3. **References that treat custom.md as the project's place for things.** Each needs a new home:
   - `code.md:4`, "see custom.md for the project's medium": dropped. The repo itself shows its medium (`Cargo.toml`).
   - `prose.md:320`, project-declared types "live in its custom.md". A declared type must be committed, or a clone's title check differs from this machine's. It moves to "the project's own edit of `prose.md`".
   - `versioning.md:83`, the `+` deviation declared in `custom.md`. Same fix as `prose.md`.
   - `session-lock.md`, the lock is "turned on by custom.md". This one can stay as a `custom.md` setting, since a lock belongs to one workspace on one machine. But that would be a second mention of `custom.md`. The alternative is turning it on by editing `session-lock.md`'s own default.
4. **The term "family" goes.** `versioning.md` and `rationale.md` say "the family's agreed version", "when the family decides", and "the family converging". The set already has the vocabulary for this: set, adopter, maintainer, convergence. The adoption bullet (`versioning.md:201`) drops `-c` and "the family's custom.md". The code keeps `-c` until the Todo entry "The family leaves the committed config" removes it.
5. **The terminology** in `AGENTS.md` loses `custom.md` from "Agent-files", and drops "Project layer" entirely.
6. **`rationale.md` follows the rules it explains.** The `## custom.md` rationale is rewritten for the new rule: public repos, and a file that belongs to one machine. The rationales for "adoption copies custom.md" and the custom.md parts of "adopted ahead" go with those rules. Old SHA links in history are harmless to keep.

**The two design questions**

- **Where do committed project-only changes go?** Today "intent picks the file": a change for the whole set edits the agent-file, and a change for this project only goes in `custom.md`. With `custom.md` local, the only committed place left is the agent-file itself. Then an adopter's diff from the template mixes proposals with permanent local divergences, and at convergence the maintainer can't tell which is which. Options:
  - **Mark a divergence where it sits (my pick).** A short "Project-only:" lead-in on the edited text, so the diff shows its intent and convergence skips those lines. It's small, greppable, and needs no new file.
  - Have the project's cycle titles or `TODO.md` record which diffs are local. That's weaker, since the diff no longer explains itself.
  - Add a committed project file under another name. That just brings `custom.md` back, so I'd avoid it.
- **What does the template ship?** That's the open bullet in the Todo entry. I'd ship no `custom.md` at all and let the one-rule section say what it's for. An example file is one more thing to keep in sync.

**Cycle mechanics**
- **Title:** `agent-files(proposal): v0.3.0`. The patch digit rolls over from v0.2.9, per the one-digit rule. The bookmark is `agent-files-proposal-v030`.
- **Version files:** `agent-data/agent-files-v0.2.9` is renamed to `-v0.3.0-0` at the opening and to bare `v0.3.0` at the close-out. The artifact's version moves beside it.
- **Shape:** single-step with a local ladder, I think. The local commits would be `AGENTS.md`, then `agent-data/` excluding the rationale, then `rationale.md`, each reviewed and then collapsed into one commit. It's one change, but 9 files is too much to review in one diff.
- **Acceptance check:**
  - `grep -n -i 'family\|custom\.md'` over `AGENTS.md` and `agent-data/*` prints only the one-rule section, the index line, the Acquaint link, and the rationale of that rule.
  - `validate-anchors` passes on all of them.
- **Close-out:**
  - It adds a row to `notes/agent-files-size.md`, since agent-files changed; the line count should drop.
  - Being a proposal, it goes out to the other members through the messages repo. Their `custom.md` files are still committed in their repos, and adopting v0.3.0 means they untrack theirs too, which is their call.

The plain version: replace every `custom.md` and "family" mention with one sentence ("if it exists, it's read first and wins"), and strip the boilerplate. The one real decision is where a project puts committed changes meant only for itself. I'd keep them in the agent-files with a "Project-only:" marker. Then it's one proposal cycle, v0.3.0, reviewed in three local steps.

**The project-only question goes away.** A change for this project is a cycle that edits the agent-file it belongs in, like any other change. No marker, no special file. The proposal needs no position on it, because the one rule works either way. ## Changing the agent-files

The official copies are the template repository's payload, and every adopter carries its own
copy ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#changing-the-agent-files)).

- Payload read-only: only a *correction* (a factual error, a typo, a stale cross-reference) goes
  straight in.
- Intent picks the file: a rule change meant for the set goes into the local copy of the agent-file
  it lives in, reviewed at convergence on the diff. One meant for this project only goes to
  `custom.md` and says why.
- Diff is the proposal: the diff between an adopter and the payload *is* its open proposal set.
- Own commit, own cycle: an agent-file change is its own commit, and convention work is its own
  cycle. A convention itch mid-feature becomes a backlog entry, never an inserted rung.
- Local experiments: a local agent-file may hold an unagreed experiment. Diff against the payload
  when that matters.
- Convergence: the maintainer reviews the adopters' diffs, folds what it accepts into the payload,
  and every adopter re-syncs.
- Retirement: a resolved experiment retires like a finished Todo, adopted and rejected alike: the
  cycle that resolved it is its record.
- Adopted ahead: a rule adopted ahead of its convention cycle lives in the agent-file it belongs
  to, never in a holding section of the project layer.

## custom.md

[custom.md](custom.md) is the project's own layer and is never universal
([why](agent-data/rationale.md#custommd)). It ships holding only its own shape, and a project adds
what it needs. Anyone may change any agent-file. custom.md is provided so an adopter can experiment
with, or override, a rule in one file when that is practical, and keep its other agent-files
identical to the payload's, so a re-sync is a copy:

- Overriding: a rule the adopter cannot keep as written goes under `## Project conventions and
  overrides`, naming the section it supersedes.
- Editing instead: an adopter with reasons custom.md cannot serve edits the agent-files directly,
  and its diff from the payload is its proposal ([Changing the
  agent-files](#changing-the-agent-files)). Defining what the set itself is, as its first adopters
  are doing, is one such reason. Such an adopter's custom.md holds pointers to project files and
  nothing else, and `## Project conventions and overrides` stays `_None._`.
- Pointer entries: an entry that only points at a further file owes no justification, and an
  agent-file asking for something "in custom.md" is answered by following the pointer.
- Precedence: custom.md is loaded last and wins conflicts with the other agent-files.

([why](agent-data/rationale.md#custommd)). It ships holding only its own shape, and a project adds
what it needs. Anyone may change any agent-file. custom.md is provided so an adopter can experiment
with, or override, a rule in one file when that is practical, and keep its other agent-files
identical to the payload's, so a re-sync is a copy:

- Overriding: a rule the adopter cannot keep as written goes under `## Project conventions and
  overrides`, naming the section it supersedes.
- Editing instead: an adopter with reasons custom.md cannot serve edits the agent-files directly,
  and its diff from the payload is its proposal ([Changing the
  agent-files](#changing-the-agent-files)). Defining what the set itself is, as its first adopters
  are doing, is one such reason. Such an adopter's custom.md holds pointers to project files and
  nothing else, and `## Project conventions and overrides` stays `_None._`.
- Pointer entries: an entry that only points at a further file owes no justification, and an
  agent-file asking for something "in custom.md" is answered by following the pointer.
- Precedence: custom.md is loaded last and wins conflicts with the other agent-files.

content.content:
# The session lock

An optional rule, off unless a project's [custom.md](../custom.md) turns it on: an agent session
holds an exclusive `flock` on `.agent-running` at the workspace root for as long as it runs, so a
second session started in the same workspace stops at its acquaint.

Universal file, shared with the template repository. A proposed change is edited here and converges
at the template ([Changing the agent-files](../AGENTS.md#changing-the-agent-files)).

## The instruction

Turning the lock on is two edits: this entry goes into
`custom.md > ## Project conventions and overrides`, first in its list and in place of the entry
that says the lock is off, and `/.agent-running` goes into the work-repo's `.gitignore`.

```
- Lock: at acquaint, before anything else, a session runs `flock -xn .agent-running true` at the
  workspace root, alone. If it fails, the session responds with the one sentence "Another session
  holds `.agent-running`, stopping." and runs no further command, not even to find the holder. If
  it succeeds, the session starts `flock -xn .agent-running sleep infinity` as a background
  command, leaves it running, and says "Lock taken." If that command exits while the session
  runs, the same sentence and the same stop. A session that already holds one does neither. A
  resumed session is told its holder was stopped with the earlier process, and it runs both
  again before anything else, as at acquaint. This keeps a second session from working in the
  workspace, so two cannot push or amend at once.
```

Turning it off is putting back the entry that says the lock is off and points here.

## What is known
44 session-lock.md
===
  `v` is the name-plus-version pair as cargo prints it (`bar v1.0.0`), and a tool's own banner stays
  bare (`vc-x1 0.82.0`), so a `v` number is the set's and a bare one the artifact's.
- **Proposals bump, adoptions copy**: a proposal cycle bumps it at the opening, advancing per
  [Advancing X.Y.Z](#advancing-xyz-patch-by-default), and its rungs walk the [Suffix
  scheme](#suffix-scheme) beside the artifact's version, `-0`, `-1`, then bare at the close-out, so
  a set copied from a draft bookmark says on its face that it is unfinished. An adoption copies the
  source's bare file and bumps nothing.
- **An adoption is a copy and a check**: `vc-x1 agent-files copy -c <src>` takes the set and the
  family's `custom.md` with it, and `vc-x1 agent-files diff -c <src>` is the adoption's last act,
  exiting zero when the two copies are the same. An adopter that keeps a `custom.md` of its own
  drops the `-c` from both, which is its prerogative.
- **Agreed**: the payload's number is the family's agreed version. An adopter ahead of it is
  proposing, one behind has not re-synced, and two proposers claiming one number are settled by the
  maintainer at convergence, the loser re-proposing under the next.
- **Which digit**: tend toward the patch digit, kept to one digit and rolled over into the minor.
  We think the minor stays within two digits and major increments when the family decides.

# Code conventions

Conventions for source code. Read this before writing code. The Rust-specific sections apply
wherever the medium is a Rust crate.

Universal file, shared with the template repository. A proposed change is edited here and converges
at the template ([Changing the agent-files](../AGENTS.md#changing-the-agent-files)).


#### Project-declared types

Beyond the common types, a project may declare its own when a recurring kind of work deserves one
searchable token. The declaration names the type, its scope vocabulary, and its description
grammar, so a reader can parse the titles and a title check can admit them by name, and the scope
slot then carries what the declaration says rather than a component. A project's own declarations
- **`+` is reserved** for the PEP 440 remap: no SemVer build-metadata use in Rust repos even though
  Cargo allows it, since spending `+` there breaks the bijection with the Python spelling. A repo
  that truly needs it declares the deviation in its `custom.md`.

## Recording the version-of-record

The second local-ladder step is ready for review: `jj diff -r nwuuktrt`. One part of the plan didn't hold up, the session lock, and I need your call on it.

**Done in this step:**
- **Boilerplate**: "Project-local content goes in custom.md" is removed from `code.md`, `jj.md`, `notes.md`, `prose.md`, `versioning.md`, and `session-lock.md`.
- **`code.md`**: the medium line no longer points at `custom.md`. It now just says the Rust sections apply wherever the medium is a Rust crate.
- **`prose.md`**:
  - A project declares its own commit types "here, in its own copy of this file".

**Not done yet, the session lock.** The plan was to turn it on by editing `session-lock.md`'s own default. But the lock has to take effect at acquaint, before anything else, and nothing tells an acquainting agent to read `session-lock.md`. Today it works because the instruction is pasted into `custom.md`, which Acquaint reads first. Two options:

- **A (my pick):** turning the lock on puts the instruction into `AGENTS.md > Acquaint` as a step before step 1, and adds `/.agent-running` to `.gitignore`. Turning it off removes that step. This follows your rule that a project's change is a cycle that edits the agent-files, and `custom.md` isn't mentioned again.
- **B:** keep `custom.md` as the switch. The lock belongs to one workspace on one machine, which is exactly what `custom.md` now is. But it's a second mention of `custom.md`, which goes against the one-mention goal.

Which do you want? Rung three, `rationale.md`, comes after this.

Bringing the mention back makes sense, but I'd change the wording in three ways:

1. **Don't link to the file.** `[custom.md](../custom.md)` is a broken link in every clone now, since the file is untracked. Write `custom.md` as code and link to the rule instead: `([custom.md](../AGENTS.md#custommd))`.
2. **Say "local", not "project-local".** `custom.md` is no longer committed, so whatever goes in it is local to this workspace on this machine, not shared by the project. A clone never sees it. Anything every clone should get, like a declared commit type or the `+` deviation, still has to go in the agent-file itself, as I did in `prose.md` and `versioning.md`. Calling it "project-local" would point people at the wrong place for those.
3. **Phrase it as a place.** "An option for project-local content is in custom.md" reads as if an option is defined inside `custom.md`.

please review

# The session lock

An optional rule, off unless a project's [custom.md](../custom.md) turns it on: an agent session
holds an exclusive `flock` on `.agent-running` at the workspace root for as long as it runs, so a
second session started in the same workspace stops at its acquaint.

Universal file, shared with the template repository. A proposed change is edited here and converges
at the template ([Changing the agent-files](../AGENTS.md#changing-the-agent-files)).

## The instruction

Turning the lock on is two edits: this entry goes into
`custom.md > ## Project conventions and overrides`, first in its list and in place of the entry
that says the lock is off, and `/.agent-running` goes into the work-repo's `.gitignore`.

```
- Lock: at acquaint, before anything else, a session runs `flock -xn .agent-running true` at the
  workspace root, alone. If it fails, the session responds with the one sentence "Another session
  holds `.agent-running`, stopping." and runs no further command, not even to find the holder. If
  it succeeds, the session starts `flock -xn .agent-running sleep infinity` as a background
  command, leaves it running, and says "Lock taken." If that command exits while the session
  runs, the same sentence and the same stop. A session that already holds one does neither. A
  resumed session is told its holder was stopped with the earlier process, and it runs both
  again before anything else, as at acquaint. This keeps a second session from working in the
  workspace, so two cannot push or amend at once.
```

Turning it off is putting back the entry that says the lock is off and points here.

## What is known

- Nothing releases the lock. The kernel drops a `flock` when the process holding it exits, and
  the session's background commands end when the session does.
- It closes no race and needs none closed: a `flock` has one winner whoever asks. A session that
  loses between its probe and its holder learns of it seconds later, when the holder exits.
- Its weakness is that an agent has to read the instruction and follow it.
- The instruction has two faults, and neither has a fix:
  - A session that has forgotten it holds the lock probes again at a reacquaint, fails against
    its own holder, and stops as if another session held it.
  - An edit to the instruction reaches only the sessions started after it.
- The tool is Linux's: macOS has the `flock` call and does not ship the tool, and Windows has
  neither.
- Without the lock, two sessions working in one workspace lose no data and leave a wrong record
  (tested 2026-10-12), and one session per workspace is the user's to keep.

The last finished cycle's record, whole. A cycle's closing replaces this file's `## Closed` with
its own block from [zDOING.md](zDOING.md) and this file's references with that block's, so the

### agent-files(proposal): v0.3.0

(wink + agent, 2026-10-17, opened 2026-10-18) The cycle **chore: custom.md is untracked and
gitignored** took `custom.md` out of the tree, so anyone can clone this public repo without
inheriting one machine's layer. The agent-files still read as if every project has a `custom.md`
and belongs to a family: the rule **Read custom.md first**, [Acquaint](AGENTS.md#acquaint)'s first
step, [custom.md](AGENTS.md#custommd), and the family's terms across `agent-data/`.

  exists it is read first, and it overrides anything in the agent-files.

  the place for one, and nothing marks a change as project-only, wink's call.
- The template's shape is TBD, its work in progress. We think its `main` will carry no `custom.md`
  and a branch the family's, and the one rule holds either way.

  switch is no second mention.

  `rationale.md`.

the family's terms replaced by the set's own, adopter, maintainer, and convergence.

`session-lock.md` now presents the lock as an experiment.

- **Intro:**
  > An experiment, not a rule of the set: an agent session holds an exclusive `flock` on `.agent-running` … It was tried and it works, but the added complication is not worth it (wink, 2026-10-18), so the set does not use it.   - Off: take the entry or pointer out of `custom.md`.
- **Unchanged:** the instruction block itself and "What is known".

## Changing the agent-files

An adopter's diff against the template repository's payload is what that adopter has proposed, so
drift is a diff, not a mystery: the proposal set needs no maintenance and cannot go stale.

**A correction goes straight into the payload** because a wrong fact has no second opinion to
gather, and leaving it in place misleads every adopter on first read.

**An agent-file change is its own commit** so `git log -- AGENTS.md agent-data/` reads as a list of
rule changes rather than unrelated feature titles, and the commit's `ochid:` trailer links the
agent-repo session that reasoned it out. The diff says what differs now. The history says when, by
whom, and why.

**Convention work runs as its own cycle** because rung by rung, rule changes bury a feature cycle's
records under work its title never promised.

**A rule adopted ahead lives in the agent-file, never a holding section**, because an adopter that
collects adopted-ahead rules in `custom.md` hides them from the one review that decides them, and a
session that skips the project layer misses binding behavior. Both measured, 2026-08-19 to
2026-08-21, when one member's project layer (`custom-family.md`) held the family's messaging rules
and the validation commands, retired by the 0.80.0 cycle, chores-17's [docs: empty custom-family
into the pinned set and

## custom.md

It ships holding nothing but its own shape so a project that changes nothing still has a valid one.
Overriding and editing are both named (wink, 2026-08-27) because the earlier text read as if every
adopter put its changes here, when custom.md alone is not always capable enough: while the set
itself is being defined, its first adopters edit the agent-files directly, and the diff against the
payload is the review that decides each change, which an override here would hide from exactly
that review. An adopter with no such reason overrides here, its honest record of where it departs,
and keeping its other agent-files identical to the payload's is what lets it re-sync by copying.
No agent-file is special: anyone can change any of them, and custom.md is only a convention that
makes overriding simpler than editing, and one file the place to distribute a project's changes
when that is practical. A pointer entry owes no
justification because it supersedes nothing, and holding a wider context behind one pointer keeps
the rest of the file identical to the payload's.

# Closed: the last cycle's record

The last finished cycle's record, whole. A cycle's closing replaces this file's `## Closed` with
its own block from [zDOING.md](zDOING.md) and this file's references with that block's, so the
last record stays here until the next one is finished. Earlier cycles are in each landmark
commit's copy of the record.

## Closed

### agent-files(proposal): v0.3.0

(wink + agent, 2026-10-17, opened 2026-10-18) The cycle **chore: custom.md is untracked and
gitignored** took `custom.md` out of the tree, so anyone can clone this public repo without
inheriting one machine's layer. The agent-files still read as if every project has a `custom.md`
and belongs to a family: the rule **Read custom.md first**, [Acquaint](AGENTS.md#acquaint)'s first
step, [custom.md](AGENTS.md#custommd), and the family's terms across `agent-data/`.

#### Deliberation

- Every mention of the family or of `custom.md` leaves the agent-files but one: when a `custom.md`
  exists it is read first, and it overrides anything in the agent-files.
- A project's own change to the agent-files is a cycle like any other, so `custom.md` stops being
  the place for one, and nothing marks a change as project-only, wink's call.
- The template's shape is TBD, its work in progress. We think its `main` will carry no `custom.md`
  and a branch the family's, and the one rule holds either way.
- The rule says it once, at the top of `AGENTS.md` and in its section: the agent must read a
  `custom.md` first, it overrides the agent-files, and it is the suggested home of most or all
  local changes. A line in each `agent-data/` file's boilerplate saying the same was tried and
  dropped, once being enough, wink's call.
- The session lock becomes an experiment the set does not use: it works, and the complication is
  not worth it, wink's call. A workspace that wants it has its `custom.md` point at
  `session-lock.md` or carry the instruction, so that file names `custom.md` too.
- Single-step, reviewed as a local ladder: `AGENTS.md`, then `agent-data/` but the rationale, then
  `rationale.md`.

#### Solution

Provisional: one rule in `AGENTS.md > ## custom.md`, which the rules index and Acquaint link, and
the family's terms replaced by the set's own, adopter, maintainer, and convergence.

#### Acceptance check

- `grep -n -i 'family\|custom\.md' AGENTS.md agent-data/*.md` prints only the one rule, its index
  line, Acquaint's link, `session-lock.md`'s switch, and that rule's rationale, and no line links
  to `custom.md`.

Yes, on both counts.

- **The bookmark already exists.** The opening published `agent-files-proposal-v030` on origin, still at `main` (`8b9b825`). The push moves it forward to the cycle's one commit, so no new bookmark is needed.
- **It's single-step.** The three `local:` commits above `main` (`nysxkqll`, `nwuuktrt`, `ztzlropr`) are the local ladder: scratch commits for review that never leave this machine. Before the push they collapse into one change: `jj squash --from 'nysxkqll::nwuuktrt' --into @`, then clearing the scratch title. That leaves a single working-copy change on `main`, with no description, holding the whole diff. Then `vc-x1 push agent-files-proposal-v030` commits it as `agent-files(proposal): v0.3.0` in both repos and pushes the bookmark.

**Order from here:**
1. On your "continue", squash the ladder.
2. Finish the close-out in the record:
   - the acceptance result
   - the final Solution
   - the closing rung flipped to `(done)`
   - a row in `notes/agent-files-size.md`
3. Run full validation.
4. Show you the title and body for the description review.
5. Push on your go.

After that come your post-push check, if you want one, and Land.
