The second local-ladder step is ready for review: `jj diff -r nwuuktrt`. One part of the plan didn't hold up, the session lock, and I need your call on it.

**Done in this step:**
- **Boilerplate**: "Project-local content goes in custom.md" is removed from `code.md`, `jj.md`, `notes.md`, `prose.md`, `versioning.md`, and `session-lock.md`.
- **`code.md`**: the medium line no longer points at `custom.md`. It now just says the Rust sections apply wherever the medium is a Rust crate.
- **`prose.md`**:
  - A project declares its own commit types "here, in its own copy of this file".
  - The semicolon sweep's list of agent-files drops `custom*`.
- **`versioning.md`**:
  - The `+` deviation is declared in the project's own copy of the file.
  - The adoption bullet drops `-c` and "the family's custom.md".
  - "Family" became "the adopters' agreed version" and "when the maintainer decides".
- **Checks**: fast validation passes, and anchors across all 12 files report 0 failed.

**Not done yet, the session lock.** The plan was to turn it on by editing `session-lock.md`'s own default. But the lock has to take effect at acquaint, before anything else, and nothing tells an acquainting agent to read `session-lock.md`. Today it works because the instruction is pasted into `custom.md`, which Acquaint reads first. Two options:

- **A (my pick):** turning the lock on puts the instruction into `AGENTS.md > Acquaint` as a step before step 1, and adds `/.agent-running` to `.gitignore`. Turning it off removes that step. This follows your rule that a project's change is a cycle that edits the agent-files, and `custom.md` isn't mentioned again.
- **B:** keep `custom.md` as the switch. The lock belongs to one workspace on one machine, which is exactly what `custom.md` now is. But it's a second mention of `custom.md`, which goes against the one-mention goal.

Which do you want? Rung three, `rationale.md`, comes after this.

please review

Bringing the mention back makes sense, but I'd change the wording in three ways:

1. **Don't link to the file.** `[custom.md](../custom.md)` is a broken link in every clone now, since the file is untracked. Write `custom.md` as code and link to the rule instead: `([custom.md](../AGENTS.md#custommd))`.
2. **Say "local", not "project-local".** `custom.md` is no longer committed, so whatever goes in it is local to this workspace on this machine, not shared by the project. A clone never sees it. Anything every clone should get, like a declared commit type or the `+` deviation, still has to go in the agent-file itself, as I did in `prose.md` and `versioning.md`. Calling it "project-local" would point people at the wrong place for those.
3. **Phrase it as a place.** "An option for project-local content is in custom.md" reads as if an option is defined inside `custom.md`.

So I'd suggest:

> Local content, for this workspace alone, may go in a `custom.md` ([custom.md](../AGENTS.md#custommd)).

**Knock-on effects:**
- **Session lock**: this settles it as option B. Once `custom.md` is the accepted place for local content, the lock switch can stay there, and since a lock belongs to one workspace that's where it fits. `session-lock.md`'s two mentions change to code spans. Its instruction is unchanged: it goes into a `custom.md` (no longer "under `## Project conventions and overrides`", since that heading belonged to the template's `custom.md` shape).
- **The rule in `AGENTS.md`** gains half a sentence to match: "…and holds what is local to the workspace."
- **The acceptance check** changes from "only the one rule" to: every remaining mention is the rule, its index and Acquaint links, the boilerplate line, `session-lock.md`'s switch, and the rule's rationale, with no `[...](custom.md)` link anywhere.
- **"Family"** still goes completely.

Should I apply that wording to the seven boilerplate lines (the six files plus `rationale.md` in the next step), and to `session-lock.md` and the rule?

Agreed, just the name. I've dropped the comma after "content", since it splits the subject from its verb, and written the name as code like the rest of the agent-files. Applying it to the six files now.

content.content:
1	# AGENTS.md - Agent Instructions
2	
3	The universal core of the agent instructions: the dual-repo model, the hard rules, the cycle
4	protocol, and a map of the rest. One of the [agent-files](#terminology), carried by every adopter.
5	The rules are an index: each is a sentence and a link to the section that holds it, and a
6	section's why is in [rationale.md](agent-data/rationale.md) under the mirrored heading.
7	
8	## Terminology
9	
10	Repos: the two repos of [the dual-repo model](#the-dual-repo-model), "work-repo" and "agent-repo",
11	always hyphenated.
12	
13	Agent-files: the instruction set an agent reads, `AGENTS.md` and `agent-data/*`. `TODO.md` is not
14	one, since its content is the project's record, but the agent-files require that there is one, of
15	the shape in [Todo format](agent-data/notes.md#todo-format).
16	
17	Agent-files version: the set's own version, `vX.Y.Z`, the name of an empty
18	`agent-data/agent-files-vX.Y.Z` file, bumped by `agent-files` proposal cycles and copied by
19	adoptions ([Agent-files version](agent-data/versioning.md#agent-files-version)).
20	
21	Set: the agent-files as the template repository's payload carries them, the copy every adopter
22	starts from and re-syncs to. Adopter: a project carrying a copy of the set. Maintainer: whoever
23	owns the template repository and decides what the payload takes.
24	
25	Cycle: one change, run from opening to closing as one commit or a ladder of them, each made by
26	`vc-x1 push` ([Cycle protocol](#cycle-protocol)). Single-step when the problem statement has one
27	straightforward solution step, its documentation in the same commit, otherwise multi-step. Both run
28	on a bookmark under the dev name, and the shape is fixed at the cycle's first push ([Cycle
29	shape](#cycle-shape)).
30	
31	Land: the sequence that makes a cycle permanent, on the user's go at the close-out
32	([Land](agent-data/jj.md#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land)). Before it the cycle is a draft on its
33	bookmark, after it the commits are permanent.
34	
35	Trapezoid: the default close-out shape, a merge commit whose first parent is the trunk line and
36	whose second is the cycle's ladder ([Close-out shapes](agent-data/jj.md#close-out-shapes)). Names
37	both the merge commit and the figure the graph draws around it.
38	
39	Artifact: the work-repo's built product. It carries a `-dev` name while a cycle runs ([Dev artifact
40	name](agent-data/versioning.md#dev-artifact-name)) and is installed at Land.
41	
42	Rationale: a rule's why, in [rationale.md](agent-data/rationale.md) under the heading that mirrors
43	the rule's, reached by `[why](agent-data/rationale.md#<same-slug>)`. Read when changing a rule,
44	not when following one.
45	
46	## The dual-repo model
47	
48	Two separate jj-git colocated repos ([jj.md](agent-data/jj.md)), located by a `.vc-config.md`,
49	never by the current directory ([.vc-config.md](agent-data/jj.md#vc-configmd),
50	[why](agent-data/rationale.md#the-dual-repo-model)):
51	
52	1. Work-repo: the project's work product. Its directory is the workspace root, the directory
53	   holding the work-repo's `.vc-config.md`, whose `[repos] work` is `"."`.
54	2. Agent-repo: the agent's session data, in the directory that file's `[repos] agent` names, a
55	   path relative to the workspace root or an absolute one, so it may sit anywhere. Written
56	   `<agent-dir>` wherever a command below needs it, and reached by Claude Code through a symlink
57	   at `~/.claude/projects/<mangled-project-path>`, which `vc-x1 init` creates for a dual
58	   workspace and `vc-x1 symlink` creates on demand.
59	
60	## Rules
61	
62	The rules, indexed: each a one-sentence summary and a link to the section that states it, this
63	file's rules first and then the outer files' in their order ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#rules)).
64	The section is the rule, the sentence its handle. None is absolute: a rule bends only when the
65	user says so explicitly, at the moment or as a scoped delegation ([Stop and ask](#stop-and-ask) is
66	the path), and the exception is recorded in the cycle's records, naming what the bend covers and
67	what it does not, so a waiver over a cycle's pushes says whether Land is inside it. No rule bends
68	silently.
69	
70	- Read custom.md first: when a `custom.md` exists, the agent must read it first, it overrides
71	  anything in the agent-files, and it is the suggested home of most or all local changes
72	  ([custom.md](#custommd)).
73	- Acquaint before work: a session acquaints first, and what its repo check finds is reported and
74	  left as found until the user says how to proceed ([Acquaint](#acquaint)).
75	- Sync where `main` matters: a look at acquaint and a sync at the opening, the closing, and Land,
76	  each reported, and a repo held back stops the step ([Sync](#sync)).
77	- A session's rules are its own agent-files: the ones it started in, binding in every repo it
78	  writes, and another repo's rules bind only by delegation ([A session's rules are its own
79	  agent-files](#a-sessions-rules-are-its-own-agent-files)).
80	- Bookmark per cycle: a cycle runs on one topic bookmark in the work-repo, and `main` advances
81	  only when the cycle lands ([Cycles run on a bookmark](#cycles-run-on-a-bookmark)).
82	- Shape at the first push: single-step or multi-step is fixed by the cycle's first push, and a
83	  ladder lands as a trapezoid or kept separate, never squashed ([Cycle shape](#cycle-shape)).
84	- Read the step before the action: [The per-rung flow](#the-per-rung-flow) before commit work,
85	  [Before any push](#before-any-push) before a push, from the file, not from memory.
86	- Push commits: a cycle rung is committed only by `vc-x1 push` ([Committing vs
87	  pushing](#committing-vs-pushing)).
88	- Approval per push: every push needs the user's explicit approval, or an explicit waiver
89	  ([Before any push](#before-any-push)).
90	- Hard stop after the final push: after the turn's final push nothing until the user speaks,
91	  unless an explicit waiver ([At rest](#at-rest-push-stop-squash-push)).
92	- Stop and ask: on ambiguous input, on any deviation from the agreed plan, and when 5+ minutes
93	  on a simple task has produced no progress ([Stop and ask](#stop-and-ask)).
94	- Changing the agent-files: an agent-file change is its own commit and convention work its own
95	  cycle, made in the local copy of the file ([Changing the agent-files](#changing-the-agent-files)).
96	- jj, not git: version-control operations use jj ([jj basics](agent-data/jj.md#jj-basics)).
97	- No hand-written trailers: `vc-x1 push` stamps `ochid:` trailers, never write one by hand
98	  ([ochid trailers](agent-data/jj.md#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)).
99	- No re-describe without coordinating: never `jj describe` a published or trailer-carrying
100	  commit ([Re-describing](agent-data/jj.md#re-describing-coordinate-first-and-keep-the-trailer)).
101	- Prose style: durable text is in the prose form, typeable punctuation included ([Prose
102	  form](agent-data/prose.md#prose-form)).
103	- One title per step: the ladder rung and the commit title are verbatim identical
104	  ([Conventional-commit shape](agent-data/prose.md#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--commit)).
105	- Alert on unwrap: say so when introducing an `unwrap` / `expect` / `unwrap_or*` site, with its
106	  `// OK: ...` comment ([`// OK` comments](agent-data/code.md#-ok--comments-on-unwrap-calls-rust)).
107	
108	## Acquaint
109	
110	What a session does first, at its start and whenever the user says "acquaint" or "reacquaint",
111	in this order ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#acquaint)):
112	
113	1. custom.md: when there is one, read it, and do what it asks for at acquaint
114	   ([custom.md](#custommd)).
115	2. Repo check: look at each repo of the workspace for the four findings below, and report what is
116	   found before anything else. Nothing is opened, pushed, rebased, committed, or discarded until
117	   the user says how to proceed.
118	   - Not up to date: a repo whose `main` is behind, ahead of, or diverged from its remote's, as
119	     the look reports it ([Sync](#sync)), run again with `--bookmark <bookmark>` when a cycle is
120	     in flight. A look that fails is reported as the check not made.
121	   - Uncommitted work: a work-repo `@` that is not empty, as `jj st` prints it. What the
122	     continuation notes account for, the notes themselves or a rung in flight they describe, is
123	     theirs to direct at step 3, and any other change is a finding. The agent-repo's `@` holds the
124	     session's own data and is never one.
125	   - Work off `main`: commits on a bookmark, a cycle's or any other, that do not descend from the
126	     remote's `main`. The user is told, and a rebase onto `main` is suggested.
127	   - Conflicts: a conflicted commit or working copy, as `jj st` and `jj log -r 'conflicts()'` show
128	     them. The acquaint stops there and the user is informed.
129	3. TODO.md: read the acquaint slice ([File
130	   reads](agent-data/notes.md#file-reads-read-the-slice-you-need)), the continuation notes first,
131	   each acted on, filed or kept, and the section reset ([Todo
132	   format](agent-data/notes.md#todo-format)).
133	4. Report: say where things stand, the cycle in flight or the top of `## Todo`, and wait.
134	
135	## Sync
136	
137	One command, `vc-x1 sync --scope=both`, brings both repos up to date, each `main` at the commit
138	its remote's `main` is at. It runs at the moments a cycle depends on `main`, and what it prints
139	is reported ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#sync)):
140	
141	- Acquaint looks: with `--dry-run`, which moves nothing, so each repo is reported as found.
142	- Opening syncs: as its first step, which is its rung's step 0, so the cycle's bookmark is
143	  created on an up-to-date `main`.
144	- Closing syncs: at its rung's step 0, so the record and version it carries are made from an
145	  up-to-date `main`. A rung between may sync at its step 0, the agent's or the user's call.
146	- Land syncs: as its first step, and a `main` the sync moved stops the Land.
147	
148	A sync that fails or holds a repo back stops the step until the user says how to proceed, as does
149	one at a rung's step 0 that moved a `main`, and `--force` and `--rebase` are the user's to ask
150	for.
151	
152	## Cycle protocol
153	
154	How a [cycle](#terminology) runs ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#cycle-protocol)). Its record is
155	`TODO.md > ## In Progress` and nothing else ([Cycle-record](#cycle-record)). The `.vc-config.md`
156	`[validate]` table defines the commands that validate the work-repo.
157	
158	### Cycles run on a bookmark
159	
160	A cycle runs on one topic bookmark in the work-repo, created at the opening and named by the cycle
161	title's slug ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#cycles-run-on-a-bookmark)). `main` advances only when
162	the finished cycle lands on it, so development is never done on `main`, a single-step cycle
163	included. The agent-repo needs no bookmark. Commands in [Cycle
164	bookmarks](agent-data/jj.md#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land), the long-lived case in [Long-lived
165	bookmarks][llb].
166	
167	### Cycle shape
168	
169	Single-step or multi-step is decided at the opening and fixed by the cycle's first push, with the
170	one coordinated exception below ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#cycle-shape)). Before that push the
171	In Progress block may be rewritten to either shape. After it:
172	
173	- A single-step cycle is one commit, made by one push, carrying the opening's duties, the work, and
174	  the close-out's duties, titled with the bare cycle title in both repos. When the work turns out to
175	  need more steps, two choices, since the bookmark is still a draft:
176	  - land the commit as it is and run the additional work as one or more further cycles
177	  - turn the commit into the opening: amend its version-of-record to the `-0` form, re-title it with
178	    " opening" as a coordinated re-describe that keeps the `ochid:` trailer ([No re-describe without
179	    coordinating](agent-data/jj.md#re-describing-coordinate-first-and-keep-the-trailer)), and
180	    complete the cycle as multi-step.
181	- A multi-step cycle is a ladder and lands as a trapezoid or kept separate, never squashed: every
182	  rung's `ochid:` trailer is a change id, and a squash discards all but one. A ladder that shrinks
183	  to one rung still closes as a ladder, since its opening already pushed.
184	
185	### Unplanned work
186	
187	Work that arrives while a cycle runs goes one of two ways, and the user picks which
188	([why](agent-data/rationale.md#unplanned-work)):
189	
190	- A rung inserted into the ladder, usually when it is inside the cycle's subject or blocks it.
191	- A `## Todo` or `## Waiting` entry, run as its own cycle later.
192	
193	A rung inserted while the working copy already holds the next rung's edits sets those edits aside
194	as a patch first, so the inserted rung's commit carries its own change alone, and they return once
195	it has pushed.
196	
197	### Cycle-record
198	
199	A cycle's record is its `TODO.md > ## In Progress` block and nothing else, the cycle-record
200	([why](agent-data/rationale.md#cycle-record)).
201	
202	- Items: title, problem, solution, acceptance check, deliberation, and the ladder heading its rung
203	  subsections, all provisional until close-out ([The In Progress
204	  block](agent-data/notes.md#the-in-progress-block)).
205	- Life: written at the opening, revised as rungs land, finalized by the closing commit, which moves
206	  it whole to `## Closed` (a single-step cycle's one commit writes it there directly), deleted by
207	  the next opening.
208	  - `## In Progress` reads `_No cycle currently in progress._` between cycles.
209	  - The closing commit's tree carries the final form, and the file never grows.
210	- After that jj holds it: `git log --grep "<cycle title>"` finds the commits, on the title the
211	  pushed bookends carry when a rename came mid-cycle, and the landmark on `main` (the trapezoid
212	  merge, or the single-step commit) holds the finished block in its `TODO.md > ## Closed`.
213	- No backfill: a rung carries no `[[N]]` placeholder, no SHA, and no version.
214	- Never amended: a late finding about a closed cycle is recorded where it is found, citing the
215	  landmark.
216	- Design findings that must outlive the cycle go into a `notes/` file by the rung that made them,
217	  never left in the block.
218	- Frozen history: `notes/chores/` and `notes/done.md` are never appended, still linked.
219	
220	### Opening
221	
222	The cycle's first commit, when it needs setup (a lightweight cycle starts at its first commit, which
223	then carries steps 1 and 2). A single-step cycle does all of it in its one commit, after steps 1
224	and 2 ([Cycle shape](#cycle-shape)). Before that commit ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#opening)):
225	
226	1. Sync: sync both repos ([Sync](#sync)), whatever the cycle's form.
227	2. Bookmark: create and publish the cycle's bookmark, a push that needs approval.
228	3. Waiting: check each `## Waiting` entry's condition, and promote what is met into `## Todo` at
229	   the rank it names.
230	4. In Progress block: delete whatever `## Closed` holds, then move the chosen `## Todo` entry into
231	   `## In Progress`, shaped as [The In Progress block](agent-data/notes.md#the-in-progress-block)
232	   says, the specimen in [cycle-model.md](agent-data/cycle-model.md).
233	5. Bump: bump the version-of-record to the opening's version ([Suffix
234	   scheme](agent-data/versioning.md#suffix-scheme)), and the agent-files version with it when the
235	   cycle is an `agent-files` proposal ([Agent-files
236	   version](agent-data/versioning.md#agent-files-version)).
237	6. Rename: when the built artifact has consumers, rename `<name>` to `<name>-dev` ([Dev artifact
238	   name](agent-data/versioning.md#dev-artifact-name)). Land restores it.
239	
240	Rungs are named, not numbered ([Steps are named, not numbered][snn]), and a multi-step cycle's
241	bookends are the cycle title plus " opening" and " closing" ([Cycle bookend titles][cbt]).
242	
243	### The per-rung flow
244	
245	Every commit (opening, each rung between, closing) goes through these steps, read from here
246	immediately before acting ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#the-per-rung-flow)):
247	
248	0. Sync: sync both repos ([Sync](#sync)), required at the opening and the closing, optional
249	   between, the agent's or the user's call.
250	1. Mark current: mark the rung `(current)` in `TODO.md > ## In Progress`, as the first edit.
251	2. Bump: bump the version-of-record to this commit's version ([Suffix
252	   scheme](agent-data/versioning.md#suffix-scheme)), the agent-files version beside it in an
253	   `agent-files` proposal cycle.
254	3. Work: do the work. On any deviation from the agreed plan, or any question, stop ([Stop and
255	   ask](#stop-and-ask)).
256	4. Rung subsection: write what this rung changed, conceptually, into its subsection under the
257	   ladder. The rung stays `(current)` until step 7.
258	5. Validate: `vc-x1 validate` before every review, doc-only commits included. The full run rewrites
259	   files (`cargo fmt`), so use `--fast` while a review iterates. A failure is read and its cause
260	   named before validation runs again, and a failure that does not repeat is a finding, reported
261	   and given a Todo entry.
262	6. Work review: stop before writing any description and say "please review", as its own message with
263	   no title or body. Iterate until the user says "continue" / "go". The review is of the
264	   working-copy diff ([jj basics](agent-data/jj.md#jj-basics)).
265	7. Flip and describe: flip `(current)` to `(done)` the moment "done" is true, then write the
266	   description in [Commit-body form](agent-data/prose.md#commit-body-form), read from the file first
267	   with its specimen, [commit-model.md](agent-data/commit-model.md) ([Commit
268	   description](#commit-description)).
269	8. Description review: show the title + body and stop. Ask permission to commit and push without
270	   spelling out the invocation. The go covers the push only when it says so.
271	9. Commit + push: on the go, `vc-x1 push <bookmark> --title "..." --body "..."` ([Committing vs
272	   pushing](#committing-vs-pushing)), then [At rest](#at-rest-push-stop-squash-push).
273	
274	### Committing vs pushing
275	
276	A cycle rung is committed *by* `vc-x1 push`, never pre-committed with `jj commit`
277	([why](agent-data/rationale.md#committing-vs-pushing)). "Commit", "push",
278	and "commit + push" all mean `vc-x1 push`. A bare `jj commit` is asked for by name and is for local
279	saves and [local ladder](#local-ladders) intermediates. What push does is in [vc-x1 push][vpush].
280	
281	### Commit description
282	
283	The title is a Conventional Commit, distinct within its cycle ([Commit titles and
284	descriptions][cdd]).
285	The body is in [Commit-body form](agent-data/prose.md#commit-body-form): no version, file list, or
286	deliberation ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#commit-description)).
287	
288	### Pushing
289	
290	Pushing is by `vc-x1 push`. The bookmark moves (create, land, trapezoid) use `jj git push` as jj.md
291	names, until vc-x1 owns them.
292	
293	#### Before any push
294	
295	([why](agent-data/rationale.md#before-any-push))
296	
297	- This specific push has the user's explicit approval, or an explicit waiver covers it.
298	- Validation ran, and passed, after the last edit.
299	- Closing words are written. Nothing follows the turn's final push.
300	
301	#### At rest: push, stop, squash-push
302	
303	The contract that keeps both repos clean, the rule **Hard stop after the final push** its first
304	item's tail ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#at-rest-push-stop-squash-push)):
305	
306	1. The agent publishes: completing a step means issuing its publishing command. The agent says what
307	   is worth saying *before* the final publishing command, responds with the one word "Published",
308	   and does nothing further until the user speaks.
309	2. The user squash-pushes: `vc-x1 squash-push -R <agent-dir>` whenever they want both repos fully
310	   pushed.
311	
312	"Clean" means both repos' `@` empty. A late work-repo tweak after the push is a remote rewrite and
313	takes approval like any push ([vc-x1 push][vpush]).
314	
315	### Close-out
316	
317	The cycle's last commit is bookkeeping and its body describes that bookkeeping. A single-step cycle
318	does all of it in its one commit, step 5 aside ([Cycle shape](#cycle-shape)):
319	
320	1. Acceptance check: run the check the opening stated and record pass or fail. A failure is a
321	   finding, and why it failed is determined.
322	2. Finalize the cycle-record in place ([Cycle-record](#cycle-record)):
323	   - sync the title if the scope shifted, and every anchor back-reference with it. A pushed rung
324	     title and the bookend pair keep their names, since retitling one is a re-describe of a
325	     published commit, so a rename mid-cycle reaches the block's text and the unpushed rungs only
326	   - replace the provisional solution statement with what was done
327	   - add the design subsections the deliberation grew
328	   - complete the closing rung's subsection
329	   - ask what in the block must outlive the cycle, and write it into the `notes/` file it
330	     belongs to
331	   - move the block whole to `## Closed`, leaving `## In Progress` reading
332	     `_No cycle currently in progress._`.
333	3. Validate: full validation, and update `notes/README.md` if functionality changed.
334	4. Size: when an agent-file changed, record the line count in `notes/agent-files-size.md`,
335	   smaller being the quasi-goal. A cycle that touched none adds no row.
336	5. Close-out shape ([Close-out shapes](agent-data/jj.md#close-out-shapes)):
337	   - choose with the user: trapezoid (the default) or keep separate
338	   - record the choice in the closing rung's subsection
339	   - reshape nothing yet, Land does.
340	6. Land: on the user's go, sync ([Sync](#sync)), restore the plain name, reshape per the choice,
341	   fast-forward `main`, install the artifact, delete the bookmark locally and remotely ([Bookmark
342	   per cycle](#cycles-run-on-a-bookmark),
343	   [Land](agent-data/jj.md#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land)).
344	7. Restart: the user restarts the agent, and before the exit anything the next agent needs is
345	   written into `TODO.md > ## Continuation notes`, the first section, which the next acquaint reads
346	   first, files or keeps, and resets ([Todo format](agent-data/notes.md#todo-format)).
347	
348	### Local ladders
349	
350	A rung that wants incremental review runs as a local ladder: a chain of jj commits that never leaves
351	the machine and collapses into the rung before the cycle continues, each validated with
352	`vc-x1 validate --fast` ([Local ladders](agent-data/jj.md#local-ladders),
353	[why](agent-data/rationale.md#local-ladders)).
354	
355	[cbt]: agent-data/prose.md#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--commit
356	[cdd]: agent-data/prose.md#commit-titles-and-descriptions
357	[llb]: agent-data/jj.md#long-lived-bookmarks-merge-only-by-default-deletable-once-merged
358	[snn]: agent-data/prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered
359	[vpush]: agent-data/jj.md#vc-x1-push-what-it-does-and-does-not-do
360	
361	## Working practices
362	
363	([why](agent-data/rationale.md#working-practices))
364	
365	- One command per invocation: no bundled steps (`a && b; c`), except a genuine pipeline or a tight
366	  pair where the join is the point.
367	- Exit status: never mask a command's exit status. No piping a validating command into `tail` /
368	  `grep` (`${PIPESTATUS[0]}` when a pipe is wanted), no `&&` after a piped stage, no trailing
369	  `; echo "exit=$?"`. To report and still fail: `cmd || { rc=$?; echo failed=$rc; exit $rc; }`.
370	- Scratch files: repo-local `tmp/` (gitignored, `mkdir -p tmp` on demand). `/tmp` is for
371	  out-of-project temporaries.
372	- Slice reads: read the slice you need from long notes files. The acquaint read is `TODO.md`
373	  `offset=0, limit=60` ([notes.md](agent-data/notes.md#file-reads-read-the-slice-you-need)).
374	- https remotes: use https remotes, and check for an ssh remote first when a push dies at the
375	  network leg. A remote URL change needs the user's go.
376	- Delegate: mechanical subtasks go to lesser models (Opus/Haiku/Sonnet).
377	- No memory directory: `~/.claude/projects/<path>/memory/` is unused, the agent-files are.
378	- Speculation: mark it in durable text with "We think ..." ([Speculation
379	  marker](agent-data/prose.md#speculation-marker)).
380	- Plain synopsis: end a technical explanation in conversation with one, marked "The plain version:"
381	  ([Plain synopsis](agent-data/prose.md#plain-synopsis-after-technical-explanations)).
382	
383	### A session's rules are its own agent-files
384	
385	A session's rules are the agent-files of the project it started in, and rules living in any other
386	repo are ignored unless these files or the user direct otherwise
387	([why](agent-data/rationale.md#a-sessions-rules-are-its-own-agent-files)). So another repo's own
388	protocol (a shared store's README, another project's agent-files) governs a write to it only as
389	far as the delegation reaches, and this file's conduct rules, the step reads, the reviews, the
390	per-push approval, and the stops, bind every commit and push the session makes, in any repo,
391	cycle or not. A repo with a live agent of its own is not written at all: message its agent.
392	
393	### Stop and ask
394	
395	Stop and ask on ambiguous input, on any deviation from the agreed plan, and when 5+ minutes on a
396	simple task has produced no progress ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#stop-and-ask)).
397	
398	## Changing the agent-files
399	
400	The official copies are the template repository's payload, and every adopter carries its own
401	copy ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#changing-the-agent-files)).
402	
403	- Payload read-only: only a *correction* (a factual error, a typo, a stale cross-reference) goes
404	  straight in.
405	- Local copy: a rule change goes into the local copy of the agent-file it lives in, as a cycle like
406	  any other, and one meant for the set is reviewed at convergence on the diff.
407	- Diff is the proposal: the diff between an adopter and the payload *is* its open proposal set.
408	- Own commit, own cycle: an agent-file change is its own commit, and convention work is its own
409	  cycle. A convention itch mid-feature becomes a backlog entry, never an inserted rung.
410	- Local experiments: a local agent-file may hold an unagreed experiment. Diff against the payload
411	  when that matters.
412	- Convergence: the maintainer reviews the adopters' diffs, folds what it accepts into the payload,
413	  and every adopter re-syncs.
414	- Retirement: a resolved experiment retires like a finished Todo, adopted and rejected alike: the
415	  cycle that resolved it is its record.
416	- Adopted ahead: a rule adopted ahead of its convention cycle lives in the agent-file it belongs
417	  to.
418	
419	## custom.md
420	
421	When a `custom.md` exists at the workspace root, the agent must read it first, and it overrides
422	anything in the agent-files ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#custommd)). Most or all of the
423	workspace's local changes are suggested to reside there.
424

# AGENTS.md - Agent Instructions

The universal core of the agent instructions: the dual-repo model, the hard rules, the cycle
protocol, and a map of the rest. One of the [agent-files](#terminology), carried by every adopter.
The rules are an index: each is a sentence and a link to the section that holds it, and a
section's why is in [rationale.md](agent-data/rationale.md) under the mirrored heading.

## Terminology

Repos: the two repos of [the dual-repo model](#the-dual-repo-model), "work-repo" and "agent-repo",
always hyphenated.

Agent-files: the instruction set an agent reads, `AGENTS.md` and `agent-data/*`. `TODO.md` is not
one, since its content is the project's record, but the agent-files require that there is one, of
the shape in [Todo format](agent-data/notes.md#todo-format).

Agent-files version: the set's own version, `vX.Y.Z`, the name of an empty
`agent-data/agent-files-vX.Y.Z` file, bumped by `agent-files` proposal cycles and copied by
adoptions ([Agent-files version](agent-data/versioning.md#agent-files-version)).

Set: the agent-files as the template repository's payload carries them, the copy every adopter
starts from and re-syncs to. Adopter: a project carrying a copy of the set. Maintainer: whoever
owns the template repository and decides what the payload takes.

Cycle: one change, run from opening to closing as one commit or a ladder of them, each made by
`vc-x1 push` ([Cycle protocol](#cycle-protocol)). Single-step when the problem statement has one
straightforward solution step, its documentation in the same commit, otherwise multi-step. Both run
on a bookmark under the dev name, and the shape is fixed at the cycle's first push ([Cycle
shape](#cycle-shape)).

Land: the sequence that makes a cycle permanent, on the user's go at the close-out
([Land](agent-data/jj.md#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land)). Before it the cycle is a draft on its
bookmark, after it the commits are permanent.

Trapezoid: the default close-out shape, a merge commit whose first parent is the trunk line and
whose second is the cycle's ladder ([Close-out shapes](agent-data/jj.md#close-out-shapes)). Names
both the merge commit and the figure the graph draws around it.

Artifact: the work-repo's built product. It carries a `-dev` name while a cycle runs ([Dev artifact
name](agent-data/versioning.md#dev-artifact-name)) and is installed at Land.

Rationale: a rule's why, in [rationale.md](agent-data/rationale.md) under the heading that mirrors
the rule's, reached by `[why](agent-data/rationale.md#<same-slug>)`. Read when changing a rule,
not when following one.

## The dual-repo model

Two separate jj-git colocated repos ([jj.md](agent-data/jj.md)), located by a `.vc-config.md`,
never by the current directory ([.vc-config.md](agent-data/jj.md#vc-configmd),
[why](agent-data/rationale.md#the-dual-repo-model)):

1. Work-repo: the project's work product. Its directory is the workspace root, the directory
   holding the work-repo's `.vc-config.md`, whose `[repos] work` is `"."`.
2. Agent-repo: the agent's session data, in the directory that file's `[repos] agent` names, a
   path relative to the workspace root or an absolute one, so it may sit anywhere. Written
   `<agent-dir>` wherever a command below needs it, and reached by Claude Code through a symlink
   at `~/.claude/projects/<mangled-project-path>`, which `vc-x1 init` creates for a dual
   workspace and `vc-x1 symlink` creates on demand.

## Rules

The rules, indexed: each a one-sentence summary and a link to the section that states it, this
file's rules first and then the outer files' in their order ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#rules)).
The section is the rule, the sentence its handle. None is absolute: a rule bends only when the
user says so explicitly, at the moment or as a scoped delegation ([Stop and ask](#stop-and-ask) is
the path), and the exception is recorded in the cycle's records, naming what the bend covers and
what it does not, so a waiver over a cycle's pushes says whether Land is inside it. No rule bends
silently.

- Read custom.md first: when a `custom.md` exists, the agent must read it first, it overrides
  anything in the agent-files, and it is the suggested home of most or all local changes
  ([custom.md](#custommd)).
- Acquaint before work: a session acquaints first, and what its repo check finds is reported and
  left as found until the user says how to proceed ([Acquaint](#acquaint)).
- Sync where `main` matters: a look at acquaint and a sync at the opening, the closing, and Land,
  each reported, and a repo held back stops the step ([Sync](#sync)).
- A session's rules are its own agent-files: the ones it started in, binding in every repo it
  writes, and another repo's rules bind only by delegation ([A session's rules are its own
  agent-files](#a-sessions-rules-are-its-own-agent-files)).
- Bookmark per cycle: a cycle runs on one topic bookmark in the work-repo, and `main` advances
  only when the cycle lands ([Cycles run on a bookmark](#cycles-run-on-a-bookmark)).
- Shape at the first push: single-step or multi-step is fixed by the cycle's first push, and a
  ladder lands as a trapezoid or kept separate, never squashed ([Cycle shape](#cycle-shape)).
- Read the step before the action: [The per-rung flow](#the-per-rung-flow) before commit work,
  [Before any push](#before-any-push) before a push, from the file, not from memory.
- Push commits: a cycle rung is committed only by `vc-x1 push` ([Committing vs
  pushing](#committing-vs-pushing)).
- Approval per push: every push needs the user's explicit approval, or an explicit waiver
  ([Before any push](#before-any-push)).
- Hard stop after the final push: after the turn's final push nothing until the user speaks,
  unless an explicit waiver ([At rest](#at-rest-push-stop-squash-push)).
- Stop and ask: on ambiguous input, on any deviation from the agreed plan, and when 5+ minutes
  on a simple task has produced no progress ([Stop and ask](#stop-and-ask)).
- Changing the agent-files: an agent-file change is its own commit and convention work its own
  cycle, made in the local copy of the file ([Changing the agent-files](#changing-the-agent-files)).
- jj, not git: version-control operations use jj ([jj basics](agent-data/jj.md#jj-basics)).
- No hand-written trailers: `vc-x1 push` stamps `ochid:` trailers, never write one by hand
  ([ochid trailers](agent-data/jj.md#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)).
- No re-describe without coordinating: never `jj describe` a published or trailer-carrying
  commit ([Re-describing](agent-data/jj.md#re-describing-coordinate-first-and-keep-the-trailer)).
- Prose style: durable text is in the prose form, typeable punctuation included ([Prose
  form](agent-data/prose.md#prose-form)).
- One title per step: the ladder rung and the commit title are verbatim identical
  ([Conventional-commit shape](agent-data/prose.md#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--commit)).
- Alert on unwrap: say so when introducing an `unwrap` / `expect` / `unwrap_or*` site, with its
  `// OK: ...` comment ([`// OK` comments](agent-data/code.md#-ok--comments-on-unwrap-calls-rust)).

## Acquaint

What a session does first, at its start and whenever the user says "acquaint" or "reacquaint",
in this order ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#acquaint)):

1. custom.md: when there is one, read it, and do what it asks for at acquaint
   ([custom.md](#custommd)).
2. Repo check: look at each repo of the workspace for the four findings below, and report what is
   found before anything else. Nothing is opened, pushed, rebased, committed, or discarded until
   the user says how to proceed.
   - Not up to date: a repo whose `main` is behind, ahead of, or diverged from its remote's, as
     the look reports it ([Sync](#sync)), run again with `--bookmark <bookmark>` when a cycle is
     in flight. A look that fails is reported as the check not made.
   - Uncommitted work: a work-repo `@` that is not empty, as `jj st` prints it. What the
     continuation notes account for, the notes themselves or a rung in flight they describe, is
     theirs to direct at step 3, and any other change is a finding. The agent-repo's `@` holds the
     session's own data and is never one.
   - Work off `main`: commits on a bookmark, a cycle's or any other, that do not descend from the
     remote's `main`. The user is told, and a rebase onto `main` is suggested.
   - Conflicts: a conflicted commit or working copy, as `jj st` and `jj log -r 'conflicts()'` show
     them. The acquaint stops there and the user is informed.
3. TODO.md: read the acquaint slice ([File
   reads](agent-data/notes.md#file-reads-read-the-slice-you-need)), the continuation notes first,
   each acted on, filed or kept, and the section reset ([Todo
   format](agent-data/notes.md#todo-format)).
4. Report: say where things stand, the cycle in flight or the top of `## Todo`, and wait.

## Sync

One command, `vc-x1 sync --scope=both`, brings both repos up to date, each `main` at the commit
its remote's `main` is at. It runs at the moments a cycle depends on `main`, and what it prints
is reported ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#sync)):

- Acquaint looks: with `--dry-run`, which moves nothing, so each repo is reported as found.
- Opening syncs: as its first step, which is its rung's step 0, so the cycle's bookmark is
  created on an up-to-date `main`.
- Closing syncs: at its rung's step 0, so the record and version it carries are made from an
  up-to-date `main`. A rung between may sync at its step 0, the agent's or the user's call.
- Land syncs: as its first step, and a `main` the sync moved stops the Land.

A sync that fails or holds a repo back stops the step until the user says how to proceed, as does
one at a rung's step 0 that moved a `main`, and `--force` and `--rebase` are the user's to ask
for.

## Cycle protocol

How a [cycle](#terminology) runs ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#cycle-protocol)). Its record is
`TODO.md > ## In Progress` and nothing else ([Cycle-record](#cycle-record)). The `.vc-config.md`
`[validate]` table defines the commands that validate the work-repo.

### Cycles run on a bookmark

A cycle runs on one topic bookmark in the work-repo, created at the opening and named by the cycle
title's slug ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#cycles-run-on-a-bookmark)). `main` advances only when
the finished cycle lands on it, so development is never done on `main`, a single-step cycle
included. The agent-repo needs no bookmark. Commands in [Cycle
bookmarks](agent-data/jj.md#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land), the long-lived case in [Long-lived
bookmarks][llb].

### Cycle shape

Single-step or multi-step is decided at the opening and fixed by the cycle's first push, with the
one coordinated exception below ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#cycle-shape)). Before that push the
In Progress block may be rewritten to either shape. After it:

- A single-step cycle is one commit, made by one push, carrying the opening's duties, the work, and
  the close-out's duties, titled with the bare cycle title in both repos. When the work turns out to
  need more steps, two choices, since the bookmark is still a draft:
  - land the commit as it is and run the additional work as one or more further cycles
  - turn the commit into the opening: amend its version-of-record to the `-0` form, re-title it with
    " opening" as a coordinated re-describe that keeps the `ochid:` trailer ([No re-describe without
    coordinating](agent-data/jj.md#re-describing-coordinate-first-and-keep-the-trailer)), and
    complete the cycle as multi-step.
- A multi-step cycle is a ladder and lands as a trapezoid or kept separate, never squashed: every
  rung's `ochid:` trailer is a change id, and a squash discards all but one. A ladder that shrinks
  to one rung still closes as a ladder, since its opening already pushed.

### Unplanned work

Work that arrives while a cycle runs goes one of two ways, and the user picks which
([why](agent-data/rationale.md#unplanned-work)):

- A rung inserted into the ladder, usually when it is inside the cycle's subject or blocks it.
- A `## Todo` or `## Waiting` entry, run as its own cycle later.

A rung inserted while the working copy already holds the next rung's edits sets those edits aside
as a patch first, so the inserted rung's commit carries its own change alone, and they return once
it has pushed.

### Cycle-record

A cycle's record is its `TODO.md > ## In Progress` block and nothing else, the cycle-record
([why](agent-data/rationale.md#cycle-record)).

- Items: title, problem, solution, acceptance check, deliberation, and the ladder heading its rung
  subsections, all provisional until close-out ([The In Progress
  block](agent-data/notes.md#the-in-progress-block)).
- Life: written at the opening, revised as rungs land, finalized by the closing commit, which moves
  it whole to `## Closed` (a single-step cycle's one commit writes it there directly), deleted by
  the next opening.
  - `## In Progress` reads `_No cycle currently in progress._` between cycles.
  - The closing commit's tree carries the final form, and the file never grows.
- After that jj holds it: `git log --grep "<cycle title>"` finds the commits, on the title the
  pushed bookends carry when a rename came mid-cycle, and the landmark on `main` (the trapezoid
  merge, or the single-step commit) holds the finished block in its `TODO.md > ## Closed`.
- No backfill: a rung carries no `[[N]]` placeholder, no SHA, and no version.
- Never amended: a late finding about a closed cycle is recorded where it is found, citing the
  landmark.
- Design findings that must outlive the cycle go into a `notes/` file by the rung that made them,
  never left in the block.
- Frozen history: `notes/chores/` and `notes/done.md` are never appended, still linked.

### Opening

The cycle's first commit, when it needs setup (a lightweight cycle starts at its first commit, which
then carries steps 1 and 2). A single-step cycle does all of it in its one commit, after steps 1
and 2 ([Cycle shape](#cycle-shape)). Before that commit ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#opening)):

1. Sync: sync both repos ([Sync](#sync)), whatever the cycle's form.
2. Bookmark: create and publish the cycle's bookmark, a push that needs approval.
3. Waiting: check each `## Waiting` entry's condition, and promote what is met into `## Todo` at
   the rank it names.
4. In Progress block: delete whatever `## Closed` holds, then move the chosen `## Todo` entry into
   `## In Progress`, shaped as [The In Progress block](agent-data/notes.md#the-in-progress-block)
   says, the specimen in [cycle-model.md](agent-data/cycle-model.md).
5. Bump: bump the version-of-record to the opening's version ([Suffix
   scheme](agent-data/versioning.md#suffix-scheme)), and the agent-files version with it when the
   cycle is an `agent-files` proposal ([Agent-files
   version](agent-data/versioning.md#agent-files-version)).
6. Rename: when the built artifact has consumers, rename `<name>` to `<name>-dev` ([Dev artifact
   name](agent-data/versioning.md#dev-artifact-name)). Land restores it.

Rungs are named, not numbered ([Steps are named, not numbered][snn]), and a multi-step cycle's
bookends are the cycle title plus " opening" and " closing" ([Cycle bookend titles][cbt]).

### The per-rung flow

Every commit (opening, each rung between, closing) goes through these steps, read from here
immediately before acting ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#the-per-rung-flow)):

0. Sync: sync both repos ([Sync](#sync)), required at the opening and the closing, optional
   between, the agent's or the user's call.
1. Mark current: mark the rung `(current)` in `TODO.md > ## In Progress`, as the first edit.
2. Bump: bump the version-of-record to this commit's version ([Suffix
   scheme](agent-data/versioning.md#suffix-scheme)), the agent-files version beside it in an
   `agent-files` proposal cycle.
3. Work: do the work. On any deviation from the agreed plan, or any question, stop ([Stop and
   ask](#stop-and-ask)).
4. Rung subsection: write what this rung changed, conceptually, into its subsection under the
   ladder. The rung stays `(current)` until step 7.
5. Validate: `vc-x1 validate` before every review, doc-only commits included. The full run rewrites
   files (`cargo fmt`), so use `--fast` while a review iterates. A failure is read and its cause
   named before validation runs again, and a failure that does not repeat is a finding, reported
   and given a Todo entry.
6. Work review: stop before writing any description and say "please review", as its own message with
   no title or body. Iterate until the user says "continue" / "go". The review is of the
   working-copy diff ([jj basics](agent-data/jj.md#jj-basics)).
7. Flip and describe: flip `(current)` to `(done)` the moment "done" is true, then write the
   description in [Commit-body form](agent-data/prose.md#commit-body-form), read from the file first
   with its specimen, [commit-model.md](agent-data/commit-model.md) ([Commit
   description](#commit-description)).
8. Description review: show the title + body and stop. Ask permission to commit and push without
   spelling out the invocation. The go covers the push only when it says so.
9. Commit + push: on the go, `vc-x1 push <bookmark> --title "..." --body "..."` ([Committing vs
   pushing](#committing-vs-pushing)), then [At rest](#at-rest-push-stop-squash-push).

### Committing vs pushing

A cycle rung is committed *by* `vc-x1 push`, never pre-committed with `jj commit`
([why](agent-data/rationale.md#committing-vs-pushing)). "Commit", "push",
and "commit + push" all mean `vc-x1 push`. A bare `jj commit` is asked for by name and is for local
saves and [local ladder](#local-ladders) intermediates. What push does is in [vc-x1 push][vpush].

### Commit description

The title is a Conventional Commit, distinct within its cycle ([Commit titles and
descriptions][cdd]).
The body is in [Commit-body form](agent-data/prose.md#commit-body-form): no version, file list, or
deliberation ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#commit-description)).

### Pushing

Pushing is by `vc-x1 push`. The bookmark moves (create, land, trapezoid) use `jj git push` as jj.md
names, until vc-x1 owns them.

#### Before any push

([why](agent-data/rationale.md#before-any-push))

- This specific push has the user's explicit approval, or an explicit waiver covers it.
- Validation ran, and passed, after the last edit.
- Closing words are written. Nothing follows the turn's final push.

#### At rest: push, stop, squash-push

The contract that keeps both repos clean, the rule **Hard stop after the final push** its first
item's tail ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#at-rest-push-stop-squash-push)):

1. The agent publishes: completing a step means issuing its publishing command. The agent says what
   is worth saying *before* the final publishing command, responds with the one word "Published",
   and does nothing further until the user speaks.
2. The user squash-pushes: `vc-x1 squash-push -R <agent-dir>` whenever they want both repos fully
   pushed.

"Clean" means both repos' `@` empty. A late work-repo tweak after the push is a remote rewrite and
takes approval like any push ([vc-x1 push][vpush]).

### Close-out

The cycle's last commit is bookkeeping and its body describes that bookkeeping. A single-step cycle
does all of it in its one commit, step 5 aside ([Cycle shape](#cycle-shape)):

1. Acceptance check: run the check the opening stated and record pass or fail. A failure is a
   finding, and why it failed is determined.
2. Finalize the cycle-record in place ([Cycle-record](#cycle-record)):
   - sync the title if the scope shifted, and every anchor back-reference with it. A pushed rung
     title and the bookend pair keep their names, since retitling one is a re-describe of a
     published commit, so a rename mid-cycle reaches the block's text and the unpushed rungs only
   - replace the provisional solution statement with what was done
   - add the design subsections the deliberation grew
   - complete the closing rung's subsection
   - ask what in the block must outlive the cycle, and write it into the `notes/` file it
     belongs to
   - move the block whole to `## Closed`, leaving `## In Progress` reading
     `_No cycle currently in progress._`.
3. Validate: full validation, and update `notes/README.md` if functionality changed.
4. Size: when an agent-file changed, record the line count in `notes/agent-files-size.md`,
   smaller being the quasi-goal. A cycle that touched none adds no row.
5. Close-out shape ([Close-out shapes](agent-data/jj.md#close-out-shapes)):
   - choose with the user: trapezoid (the default) or keep separate
   - record the choice in the closing rung's subsection
   - reshape nothing yet, Land does.
6. Land: on the user's go, sync ([Sync](#sync)), restore the plain name, reshape per the choice,
   fast-forward `main`, install the artifact, delete the bookmark locally and remotely ([Bookmark
   per cycle](#cycles-run-on-a-bookmark),
   [Land](agent-data/jj.md#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land)).
7. Restart: the user restarts the agent, and before the exit anything the next agent needs is
   written into `TODO.md > ## Continuation notes`, the first section, which the next acquaint reads
   first, files or keeps, and resets ([Todo format](agent-data/notes.md#todo-format)).

### Local ladders

A rung that wants incremental review runs as a local ladder: a chain of jj commits that never leaves
the machine and collapses into the rung before the cycle continues, each validated with
`vc-x1 validate --fast` ([Local ladders](agent-data/jj.md#local-ladders),
[why](agent-data/rationale.md#local-ladders)).

## Working practices

([why](agent-data/rationale.md#working-practices))

- One command per invocation: no bundled steps (`a && b; c`), except a genuine pipeline or a tight
  pair where the join is the point.
- Exit status: never mask a command's exit status. No piping a validating command into `tail` /
  `grep` (`${PIPESTATUS[0]}` when a pipe is wanted), no `&&` after a piped stage, no trailing
  `; echo "exit=$?"`. To report and still fail: `cmd || { rc=$?; echo failed=$rc; exit $rc; }`.
- Scratch files: repo-local `tmp/` (gitignored, `mkdir -p tmp` on demand). `/tmp` is for
  out-of-project temporaries.
- Slice reads: read the slice you need from long notes files. The acquaint read is `TODO.md`
  `offset=0, limit=60` ([notes.md](agent-data/notes.md#file-reads-read-the-slice-you-need)).
- https remotes: use https remotes, and check for an ssh remote first when a push dies at the
  network leg. A remote URL change needs the user's go.
- Delegate: mechanical subtasks go to lesser models (Opus/Haiku/Sonnet).
- No memory directory: `~/.claude/projects/<path>/memory/` is unused, the agent-files are.
- Speculation: mark it in durable text with "We think ..." ([Speculation
  marker](agent-data/prose.md#speculation-marker)).
- Plain synopsis: end a technical explanation in conversation with one, marked "The plain version:"
  ([Plain synopsis](agent-data/prose.md#plain-synopsis-after-technical-explanations)).

### A session's rules are its own agent-files

A session's rules are the agent-files of the project it started in, and rules living in any other
repo are ignored unless these files or the user direct otherwise
([why](agent-data/rationale.md#a-sessions-rules-are-its-own-agent-files)). So another repo's own
protocol (a shared store's README, another project's agent-files) governs a write to it only as
far as the delegation reaches, and this file's conduct rules, the step reads, the reviews, the
per-push approval, and the stops, bind every commit and push the session makes, in any repo,
cycle or not. A repo with a live agent of its own is not written at all: message its agent.

### Stop and ask

Stop and ask on ambiguous input, on any deviation from the agreed plan, and when 5+ minutes on a
simple task has produced no progress ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#stop-and-ask)).

## Changing the agent-files

The official copies are the template repository's payload, and every adopter carries its own
copy ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#changing-the-agent-files)).

- Payload read-only: only a *correction* (a factual error, a typo, a stale cross-reference) goes
  straight in.
- Local copy: a rule change goes into the local copy of the agent-file it lives in, as a cycle like
  any other, and one meant for the set is reviewed at convergence on the diff.
- Diff is the proposal: the diff between an adopter and the payload *is* its open proposal set.
- Own commit, own cycle: an agent-file change is its own commit, and convention work is its own
  cycle. A convention itch mid-feature becomes a backlog entry, never an inserted rung.
- Local experiments: a local agent-file may hold an unagreed experiment. Diff against the payload
  when that matters.
- Convergence: the maintainer reviews the adopters' diffs, folds what it accepts into the payload,
  and every adopter re-syncs.
- Retirement: a resolved experiment retires like a finished Todo, adopted and rejected alike: the
  cycle that resolved it is its record.
- Adopted ahead: a rule adopted ahead of its convention cycle lives in the agent-file it belongs
  to.

## custom.md

When a `custom.md` exists at the workspace root, the agent must read it first, and it overrides
anything in the agent-files ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#custommd)). Most or all of the
workspace's local changes are suggested to reside there.

point at each other (the `ochid:` trailer). Read this before any jj operation beyond `st` / `log` /
`diff`, and always before touching a commit description.

## jj Basics

Conventions the agent follows when reading and writing notes files (`TODO.md`,
`notes/todo-backlog.md`, `notes/bugs.md`, and the frozen `notes/chores/chores-NN.md` and
`notes/done.md`, [Frozen history](#frozen-history-chores-and-done)). One source of truth lives here,

== prose
# Prose and durable text

How long-lived text is written on this project: the prose shape, the punctuation rules, and the
commit-title identity. Read this before writing durable text (notes files, commit messages, doc
comments, the cycle-record).

## Prose form

== prose project-declared
The common types: `feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `test`, `docs`, `chore`. A type beyond the common set
is a declared one ([Project-declared types](#project-declared-types)), and a title check admits
exactly the two vocabularies.

#### Conventional commit scopes

A scope names a component as its user would name it (a subcommand, a repo), never a file or
directory, and is omitted when there is none. A declared type's scope slot carries its
declaration's vocabulary instead ([Project-declared types](#project-declared-types)).

#### Project-declared types

Beyond the common types, a project may declare its own when a recurring kind of work deserves one
searchable token. The declaration names the type, its scope vocabulary, and its description
grammar, so a reader can parse the titles and a title check can admit them by name, and the scope
slot then carries what the declaration says rather than a component. A project declares its own
here, in its own copy of this file, and the set declares for itself:
== rationale adoption
`v` for a name paired with its version in a line (`Compiling bar v1.0.0`), and the agent-files
version is always the pair.

**The suffix walks in the file name and never in a title** because a rung's title is its ladder
line, which carries no version ([Steps are named, not
numbered](prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered)), so a proposal cycle's rungs are told apart by
the bookends while the file says at every commit whether the set is mid-cycle, which is what a copy
taken from a draft bookmark needs to say on its face.

**Proposals bump and adoptions copy** because a proposal is the diff, and the bump is part of it,
while an adoption takes a text that already has its number: the same title in two repos then reads
as the copy and its origin.

**An adoption is a copy and ends on a diff** (wink, 2026-10-13) because the diff is the proof that
the copy is whole, and it fails on a file an adopter edited after copying. Until v0.3.0 the copy
took the members' shared project layer too, under `-c`, and it stopped when that layer became local
([custom.md](#custommd)).

**Patch by default, with digit limits** (wink, 2026-09-07) because the earlier rule, patch for a
correction and minor for a rule change, would have moved the minor at nearly every proposal: a set
change is a rule change more often than not, and each is incompatible in the SemVer sense, since an
== rationale terminology
differently next time.

## Terminology

**Retired names.** "Bot repo" (2026-08-21), when the code respelled the side `agent`. "Instruction
files", an earlier name for the agent-files. "Ladder (sub-cycle)" for a local ladder, under [Local
ladders](#local-ladders). "Project layer" (2026-10-18), the project's own agent-files, retired when
the one file it named became local ([custom.md](#custommd)).

# Prose and durable text

How long-lived text is written on this project: the prose shape, the punctuation rules, and the
commit-title identity. Read this before writing durable text (notes files, commit messages, doc
comments, the cycle-record).

## Prose form

== prose project-declared
The common types: `feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `test`, `docs`, `chore`. A type beyond the common set
is a declared one ([Project-declared types](#project-declared-types)), and a title check admits
exactly the two vocabularies.

#### Conventional commit scopes

A scope names a component as its user would name it (a subcommand, a repo), never a file or
directory, and is omitted when there is none. A declared type's scope slot carries its
declaration's vocabulary instead ([Project-declared types](#project-declared-types)).

#### Project-declared types

Beyond the common types, a project may declare its own when a recurring kind of work deserves one
searchable token. The declaration names the type, its scope vocabulary, and its description
grammar, so a reader can parse the titles and a title check can admit them by name, and the scope
slot then carries what the declaration says rather than a component. A project declares its own
here, in its own copy of this file, and the set declares for itself:

content.text:
I read the set the way a new adopter would, `AGENTS.md` first and then the changed files, and I grepped for words that would be stale now (project layer, override, member, template, payload, verbatim). The core of the change holds together: the one rule, the index bullet, and Acquaint step 1 agree; Set/Adopter/Maintainer are the only actors left; `prose.md`'s declared types and the "Local copy" bullet say the same thing; no link points at `custom.md`; and `rationale.md` mirrors the new headings. But I found three places where the set now contradicts itself, and two where the rule itself is vaguer than an adopter needs.

**Contradictions, worth fixing before this goes to the family**

1. **"Diff is the proposal" overclaims now.** `AGENTS.md:407` says the diff between an adopter and the payload *is* its open proposal set, and `agent-data/rationale.md:382` repeats it. But the new "Local copy" bullet (`AGENTS.md:405`) sends project-only changes into the same files, so the diff holds proposals and permanent local divergences mixed, and nothing tells the maintainer which is which. The "Convergence" bullet already says the maintainer "folds what it accepts", so the honest sentence is: the diff is what convergence *reviews*, the adopter's proposals and its own changes alike. One sentence in each file.

2. **`versioning.md` contradicts itself.** Its intro (`agent-data/versioning.md:3-6`) says "this file is copied **verbatim**", with per-medium conditionals "rather than per-project edits". The line this cycle added (`:82`) says a repo declares its `+` deviation "here, in its own copy of this file". Both can't be true. Fix: drop the "verbatim" claim from the intro, keep the conditional point.

3. **`session-lock.md` is now an orphan in the set.** Nothing in `AGENTS.md` or any other agent-file links it; the only links are this project's `README.md`, `notes/README.md`, and `TODO.md`. Before, `custom.md` pointed at it. An adopter now finds a file in `agent-data/` that opens "An experiment, not a rule of the set" with nothing leading to it. Cheapest fix: one sentence in `AGENTS.md > ## custom.md`, "An example of local content is the session lock, `agent-data/session-lock.md`." The cleaner long-term answer is moving it out of `agent-data/` into `notes/`, since the set doesn't use it, but that's a Todo entry, not this cycle.

**The rule's wording**

4. **"most or all local changes" is vague where it matters most** (`AGENTS.md:70-72`, `:421-423`). An adopter can read "local changes" as uncommitted code. The thing we mean is *what is true of one machine or workspace*: sibling-repo paths, standing permissions, a lock switch. And "are suggested to reside there" is passive. Suggest, for the section: "When a `custom.md` exists at the workspace root, the agent must read it first, and it overrides anything in the agent-files. It is the place for what is local to the workspace, one machine's paths and permissions, since a change every clone needs is a cycle on the agent-file it belongs in." The index bullet ends "...and it holds what is local to the workspace."

5. **"A session's rules are its own agent-files"** (`AGENTS.md:383-391`) now literally excludes `custom.md`, since the terminology no longer counts it as an agent-file. The override rule covers it in practice, but one clause closes the gap: "the agent-files of the project it started in, and its `custom.md`".

**Leftover vocabulary, low**

6. "member" survives in `rationale.md` at `:399` ("one member's holding file") and `:615` ("the members' shared project layer"), undefined now that the family is gone. Both are history and read fine as "adopter". `:544` ("member-list-and-date grammar") names an old title grammar and can stay.

**Not this cycle's, noted so you know I saw them:** `AGENTS.md:155` still says the record is `TODO.md > ## In Progress` while the `zDOING.md` trial runs; `rationale.md` has no per-file section for `session-lock.md`; `code.md:73` and `jj.md:44` make claims about the WIP template's `CargoRust.toml` and `jj-tips.md`. And `TODO.md:159`'s session-lock entry has a bullet about fixing the on/off steps that this cycle partly did, so that entry wants a trim at some point.

**How to apply fixes, your call.** The commit is pushed on the bookmark, not landed. Items 1 through 5 are about eight sentences. Options:
- **Amend into the one commit (my pick).** Edit, validate, `jj squash` into `@-` (which keeps the description and its `ochid:` trailer, since `@` has none), and re-push the bookmark. That's a remote rewrite, so it takes your approval like any push, and the record gets a deliberation bullet saying the review found these. Better to send the family one coherent v0.3.0 than v0.3.0 and a v0.3.1 fix on its heels.
- **Land as is, fix in v0.3.1.** Cleaner history, but the proposal goes out with the contradictions in it.

The plain version: the change itself is sound and the vocabulary sweep is clean, but three sentences elsewhere in the set still describe the old world ("the diff is the proposal", "copied verbatim", and a lock file nothing points at), and the rule's "most or all local changes" should say what it means: what belongs to one machine. I'd fix all of it in the pushed commit before landing.

- Every mention of the family or of `custom.md` leaves the agent-files but one: when a `custom.md`
  exists it is read first, and it overrides anything in the agent-files.

  dropped, once being enough, wink's call.

  is read first and covers every agent-file, and `commit-model.md` and `cycle-model.md` never had

  not worth it, wink's call. A workspace that wants it has its `custom.md` point at

  the set or for this project alone.

  A project's own commit types and the `+` deviation are declared in its copy of `prose.md` and

- `session-lock.md` presents the lock as an experiment the set does not use, which a workspace's
  `custom.md` may point at or carry.
- The family's terms give way to the set's own, adopters and the maintainer, and `rationale.md`
  follows each rule, its `## custom.md` rewritten for the local file.
- `notes/agent-files-size.md` gains the v0.3.0 column. Its `custom.md` row, 15, is this machine's

# Closed: the last cycle's record

The last finished cycle's record, whole. A cycle's closing replaces this file's `## Closed` with
its own block from [zDOING.md](zDOING.md) and this file's references with that block's, so the
last record stays here until the next one is finished. Earlier cycles are in each landmark
commit's copy of the record.

## Closed

### agent-files(proposal): v0.3.0

(wink + agent, 2026-10-17, opened 2026-10-18) The cycle **chore: custom.md is untracked and
gitignored** took `custom.md` out of the tree, so anyone can clone this public repo without
inheriting one machine's layer. The agent-files still read as if every project has a `custom.md`
and belongs to a family: the rule **Read custom.md first**, [Acquaint](AGENTS.md#acquaint)'s first
step, [custom.md](AGENTS.md#custommd), and the family's terms across `agent-data/`.

#### Deliberation

- Every mention of the family or of `custom.md` leaves the agent-files but one: when a `custom.md`
  exists it is read first, and it overrides anything in the agent-files.
- A project's own change to the agent-files is a cycle like any other, so `custom.md` stops being
  the place for one, and nothing marks a change as project-only, wink's call.
- The template's shape is TBD, its work in progress. We think its `main` will carry no `custom.md`
  and a branch the family's, and the one rule holds either way.
- The rule says it once, at the top of `AGENTS.md` and in its section: the agent must read a
  `custom.md` first, it overrides the agent-files, and it is the suggested home of most or all
  local changes. A line in each `agent-data/` file's boilerplate saying the same was tried and
  dropped, once being enough, wink's call.
- By the same reasoning the banner itself goes, wink's call at the description review: `AGENTS.md`
  is read first and covers every agent-file, and `commit-model.md` and `cycle-model.md` never had
  one.
- The session lock becomes an experiment the set does not use: it works, and the complication is
  not worth it, wink's call. A workspace that wants it has its `custom.md` point at
  `session-lock.md` or carry the instruction, so that file names `custom.md` too.
- Single-step, reviewed as a local ladder: `AGENTS.md`, then `agent-data/` but the rationale, then
  `rationale.md`.
- A read of the whole set after the push, wink's ask, found three sentences still describing the
  old world, fixed in the pushed commit before Land: "Diff is the proposal" overclaimed once a
  project's own changes share the diff, `versioning.md` said it is copied verbatim while its `+`
  line says edit your copy, and nothing in the set linked `session-lock.md`. The rule's "most or
  all local changes" became "what is local to the workspace", and "A session's rules are its own
  agent-files" names `custom.md` beside them.

#### Solution

- `AGENTS.md` states the rule once, in `## custom.md` and its index line: when a `custom.md` exists
  the agent must read it first, it overrides anything in the agent-files, and it holds what is
  local to the workspace, the session lock its example. Acquaint's first step links it.
- The terminology drops `custom.md` from the agent-files and retires "Project layer", and
  "Changing the agent-files" makes a rule change a cycle on the local copy of its agent-file, for
  the set or for this project alone.
- The seven `agent-data/` files that opened on a "Universal file, shared with the template
  repository" banner, its last sentence "Project-local content goes in custom.md", drop it whole.
  A project's own commit types and the `+` deviation are declared in its copy of `prose.md` and
  `versioning.md`, and the adoption bullet drops `-c` and the family's `custom.md`.
- `session-lock.md` presents the lock as an experiment the set does not use, which a workspace's
  `custom.md` may point at or carry.
- The family's terms give way to the set's own, adopters and the maintainer, and `rationale.md`
  follows each rule, its `## custom.md` rewritten for the local file.
- `notes/agent-files-size.md` gains the v0.3.0 column. Its `custom.md` row, 15, is this machine's
  local file, which `vc-x1 agent-files size` still counts, so the agent-files' own total is 1829.

#### Acceptance check

- `grep -n -i 'family\|custom\.md' AGENTS.md agent-data/*.md` prints only the one rule, its index
  line, Acquaint's link, the session-rules sentence naming it, `session-lock.md`'s switch, that
  rule's rationale with the links to it, and a sha-link into history, and no line links to
  `custom.md`.
- `vc-x1 validate-anchors` passes on `AGENTS.md`, `agent-data/*.md`, `TODO.md`, and `zCLOSED.md`.
- Result: pass. The grep prints 18 lines, 7 in `AGENTS.md`, 3 in `session-lock.md`, and 8 in
  `rationale.md`, each of the allowed kinds, no line links to `custom.md`, and the anchors check
  reports 0 failed across 13 files.

#### Ladder

- agent-files(proposal): v0.3.0 (done)

# References

# Versioning

How this project versions its commits and the running artifact. The scheme, meaning the cycle suffix
spelling and the unique-per-commit aim, is generic and shared across projects, with [Recording the
version-of-record](#recording-the-version-of-record) covering each medium by conditional rather than
per-project edits.

## Terms

Three names, used as defined here across [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) and the notes files:

- **version**: the per-commit version (e.g. `0.3.0-5.3.0`). It lives in the manifest. No ladder,
  todo entry, commit title, or commit body writes one (see [Versions live in the version-of-record
  only](prose.md#versions-live-in-the-version-of-record-only)), and its suffix encodes the cycle
  phase for whoever inspects the manifest (see [Suffix scheme](#suffix-scheme)).
- **version-of-record**: the authoritative stored copy of the version, in the project's manifest
  (see [Recording the version-of-record](#recording-the-version-of-record)). A built or running
  artifact derives from it.
- **versioning**: the topic, this scheme as a whole.

## A stamp, not a name

The version answers "which commit produced this artifact". It is not a name for a step: a step is
named by its title and located by its position in the ladder list (see [Steps are named, not
numbered](prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered)). So the suffix below is the only number in the
system, and since nothing dereferences it, reordering or inserting a step leaves the versions
already committed alone.

## Advancing X.Y.Z: patch by default

Which of the three numbers moves is not a classification problem
([why](rationale.md#advancing-xyz-patch-by-default)): **patch by default, minor by the user's call,
major by the project's promise.**

- **Patch by default**: every cycle advances `Z`, whatever it touched. Code or docs, large or small,
  none of it matters, so the choice costs no deliberation.
- **Minor is deliberate and rare**: the user names it at a cycle's opening when the change deserves
  a visible marker in the history, and the agent never infers it from a change's content or size.
- **Major is a project's own call**, since what `X` promises depends on the artifact and its users.
  A project that makes that promise records it as its local edit of this rule, and absent one the
  default above governs.

## Grammar and storage

One spelling everywhere the version is written:

```
<public>[-<suffix>]
```

- `<public>`: `X.Y.Z`, integers.
- `<suffix>`: dot-separated identifiers, each ASCII letters or digits: usually integers (`3`, `3.1`,
  `3.1.0`), with an alphanumeric id (`3.hotfix`) allowed sparingly.
- **Exactly one `-` in the whole version**, the one that opens the suffix: never a dash inside the
  suffix, never a `+` in this spelling. This is the portability invariant that makes the version
  storable in every medium below ([why](rationale.md#grammar-and-storage)).
- **`v` is a display prefix, not part of the version**: conversation and reports may write
  `v0.78.0-3.1` for scannability, while manifests store the bare form. (PEP 440 ignores a leading
  `v`. Cargo rejects one.)

Storage is a per-medium remap of that one spelling:

- **SemVer mediums** (Rust/Cargo): store verbatim. The suffix rides in the prerelease slot, valid at
  any dot depth.
- **PEP 440 mediums** (Python): remap the single `-` to `+`: `0.78.0-3.1` -> `0.78.0+3.1`.
  Mechanical and bijective because there is exactly one dash to find.
- **Other mediums**: verbatim if the format allows the one `-`, else the `+` remap. A new medium
  adds its case to [Recording the version-of-record](#recording-the-version-of-record).

Two reservations keep the remap sound:

- **The stored version identifies but does not order.** SemVer sorts a suffixed version *before* its
  bare release (matching cycle semantics: rungs precede close-out), while PEP 440 sorts the remapped
  form *after* it, and reinterprets a lone `-N` as a post-release. Opposite directions, so no
  cross-medium logic may compare stored versions. Ordering truth lives in the ladder and git

running artifact identifies the exact commit it came from.

  less often: once per cycle, only at release, and so on. Record the choice in [Recording the
  version-of-record](#recording-the-version-of-record) if it differs.

  which a commit cannot contain.

The cycle (opening -> commits -> closing, per the [Cycle protocol](../AGENTS.md#cycle-protocol))
encodes each commit's phase in the version suffix, the **final identifier `0` marking a
Preparation**.

number nor a version (see [Steps are named, not numbered](prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered)).

- `X.Y.Z-3`: its Close-out
- `X.Y.Z-3.1.0`: Preparation of the `-3.1` sub-sub-cycle

so the manifest always records the commit it will be part of and, per the preference above, every
commit carries a distinct version.

The agent-files set has a version of its own, apart from the artifact's, so which set an adopter
carries is read from a listing rather than a diff, and an `agent-files` title has a token that is
unique by construction ([Project-declared types](prose.md#project-declared-types),

  `agent-files` title, and vc-x1's output, so `agent-files v0.1.0` reads the same in all three. The

  bare (`vc-x1 0.82.0`), so a `v` number is the set's and a bare one the artifact's.
- **Proposals bump, adoptions copy**: a proposal cycle bumps it at the opening, advancing per
  [Advancing X.Y.Z](#advancing-xyz-patch-by-default), and its rungs walk the [Suffix
  scheme](#suffix-scheme) beside the artifact's version, `-0`, `-1`, then bare at the close-out, so

  source's bare file and bumps nothing.
- **An adoption is a copy and a check**: `vc-x1 agent-files copy <src>` takes the set, and
  `vc-x1 agent-files diff <src>` is the adoption's last act, exiting zero when the two copies are
  the same.
- **Agreed**: the payload's number is the adopters' agreed version. An adopter ahead of it is
  proposing, one behind has not re-synced, and two proposers claiming one number are settled by the
  maintainer at convergence, the loser re-proposing under the next.
- **Which digit**: tend toward the patch digit, kept to one digit and rolled over into the minor.
  We think the minor stays within two digits and major increments when the maintainer decides.
